components.name: checkbox
components.description: Checkbox input with label, hint, and error support

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method this component should call, when it should show the new value before the server has agreed to it. Null renders the plain checkbox. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: hideLabel
props.comment: Render the label sr-only (kept as the control's accessible name) — for a checkbox in a table column whose header already names it, so the visible label is redundant. Mirrors input / select / textarea / combobox `hideLabel`.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: groupError
props.comment: Take the surrounding field.set's group error, or decline it. A control that belongs to the group but neither causes the rejection nor can resolve it says `:group-error="false"` and is then neither announced as invalid nor described by the group's message.

props.name: variant
props.comment: 'default' (inline control + label) or 'card' (the whole bordered card is the clickable target and highlights when checked — the selectable-option pattern).

components.name: color-picker
components.description: Native color picker with preview swatch

props.name: required
props.comment: `required` — DECLARED rather than left to the attribute bag. Undeclared, Blade would fold it into the bag and it would land on a wrapper div, where it is invalid HTML that nothing reads: no native constraint, no aria-required, no asterisk.

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call once a color is settled — a released drag, a swatch, an arrow-key nudge. A refusal KEEPS the color and says it was not saved: the hex field is typed, and a rollback may never delete what the reader wrote. See the note at the top of this file. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: error
props.comment: `error` and `hint` are declared: undeclared, `:error="$errors->first('brand_color')"` would land in the attribute bag and render as `error="…"` on the native `<input type="color">` — invalid HTML carrying a validation message the reader is never shown. No `label` prop comes with them, deliberately. The accessible name here is the DEFAULT SLOT (rendered `sr-only` beside the swatch, documented on the component page and sanctioned in the accessibility rules), and a second naming path would give the component two ways to be named with nothing deciding between them.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: Whether the error paragraph announces itself. Same precedence chain as every sibling control: explicit prop > the enclosing form's @aware value > config.

props.name: popover
props.comment: Popover mode — a from-scratch HSV picker (SV plane + hue + alpha + format input + swatches + eyedropper + copy + recents). Default false renders the native <input type="color">. Boolean flag (not a `mode` prop) per the prop-naming convention — same call the date-picker `range` made.

props.name: format
props.comment: hex | rgb | hsl | oklch

props.name: nativeOnMobile
props.comment: Popover mode only: on touch-primary devices (pointer: coarse) open the platform's native color sheet instead of the custom panel — the same dialog the default (non-popover) variant gets for free. Opt-in; desktop pointers always get the popover.

props.name: withClear
props.comment: Popover mode only: render a "clear" (no color) button that empties the bound form value. The native <input type="color"> cannot represent an empty value (HTML coerces it to #000000), so this is popover-only. Off by default — "no color" is rarely a valid state on a color control.

components.name: combobox
components.description: Autocomplete select with search filtering

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: Livewire method to call optimistically. The choice appears immediately and is put back if the call fails. Absent -> the plain combobox. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: placement
props.comment: Where the options panel opens against the field: any placement `dropdown` takes. The panel still flips to the other side when the chosen one has no room.

props.name: panelWidth
props.comment: How wide the panel is. `trigger` matches the field. `auto` takes the width of the widest option, and a CSS length sets one. Those two are never narrower than the field and never wider than the room the placement leaves.

props.name: searchable
props.comment: `false` renders a select-only combobox: a focusable trigger instead of a text field, for a short list nobody needs to search, with the keyboard of the WAI-ARIA select-only pattern.

props.name: freeInput
props.comment: Free input, after the WAI-ARIA editable combobox with list autocomplete: the text in the field is the value. `wire:model` binds the text, `required` checks it, `name` submits it, and the caller's `autocomplete` token stays on the field, so a browser can fill an address into it. A suggestion fills the field and says which one it was with `wirekit:combobox-choose`. For an address, a name or anything else a list cannot hold in full. Implies `searchable`.

props.name: clearable
props.comment: `false` hides the clear button. The default is true, because for most lists "none of them" is a real answer a reader must be able to give back. It is NOT one everywhere: a control whose value is a PRECONDITION for the field around it -- the country in a phone number, which is what assembles the E.164 -- ends up in a state where the reader sees a number on screen and the form submits nothing. That is the exact failure the surrounding component is usually built to prevent, so it has to be able to say no.

props.name: placeholder
props.comment: `??` rather than a `config(…, 'Select…')` fallback, and the difference is the whole point: a config default holds ONE string for every locale, so a literal in that second argument would be unreachable to a translated app, whose only escape would be publishing the config, which freezes the wording again. The seam survives (an app may still pin its own word), and an untouched default resolves through the catalog, as it does in multi-select.

props.name: hint
props.comment: `hint`, as every sibling control carries it. Undeclared, `hint="Start typing to search"` would land on the wrapper div as a stray HTML attribute: never displayed, never announced, and never reported, because Blade folds an undeclared prop into the attribute bag without complaint.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the combobox. Mirrors select / multi-select: a visible `label` renders an associated x-wirekit::label (for={comboId}); `hideLabel` keeps it in the DOM for assistive tech but visually hidden (compact toolbar / header fields); `ariaLabel` sets aria-label directly on the role="combobox" input for the label-less case. All default to no label at all.

props.name: server
props.comment: Search on the server instead of in the browser, for a list too long to render into the page. The typed text is sent as a `search-change` event with `{ value }` once it settles, and `options` are the results the application renders for it. The choice keeps its label after the results move on. Needs the search field, so it does nothing with `searchable` off.

props.name: searchMinLength
props.comment: Characters before the text is sent. Shorter text sends an empty value, once.

props.name: searchDebounce
props.comment: Milliseconds of quiet before the text is sent: one request per settled search rather than one per character. 0 sends at once, for an application that throttles on its side.

props.name: truncated
props.comment: The application cut its results at a limit. The list then says there are more.

props.name: attribution
props.comment: A line under the suggestions naming their source, as the license of their data may require: "© OpenStreetMap contributors" for suggestions from OpenStreetMap.

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: What the field says when there is nothing to choose, as on `select`: the sentence, where the missing record is created (a link after it; null for a reader who may not create one), the link's text ("Create one" without it), and whether the link moves with `wire:navigate`. Set, the combobox is disabled while there is nothing to choose and names the sentence in its aria-describedby. The `empty` slot replaces the sentence and the link.

props.name: nothingToChoose
props.comment: That there is nothing to choose. A list from `options` says it by holding no option; a server search starts every list empty, so there the application says it.

components.name: date-picker
components.description: Calendar-based date input

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: Livewire method to call optimistically. The date appears immediately and is put back if the call fails. Single-date mode only — see the note above. Absent -> the component renders without an optimistic layer. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: range
props.comment: false (default) renders one native date input. true renders a linked start + end pair (two native inputs) — see the range parsing below.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: formatHint
props.comment: Say so when the browser writes dates in a different order than the page, rather than change the order — which no author can do. A native `<input type="date">` takes its format from the BROWSER's user-interface language and from nothing else; it is not an authorable property in any shipped browser, which is why this is a disclosure and not a `locale` prop. The misreading it closes is silent, and that is what makes it worth a prop: `03.04.2026` and `04/03/2026` are both valid dates. Nothing is rejected, no error appears, and the record carries a different day than the person meant. It happens wherever the system language and the page disagree: an operator on an English laptop entering a date on a German screen is the common case. Off by default. On, it renders NOTHING when the two orders agree — the overwhelmingly common case. If you want the application's own format, the answer is a different component. `x-wirekit::calendar` takes the application locale and draws the dates itself. The trade is the one this component exists to avoid: a non-native field gives up the keyboard model, the calendar the browser opens, and the date wheel on a phone. And the name above carries no angle brackets, which is not a typo. Blade's pre-compiler scans raw text for component tags, before any of this is a PHP comment — so a tag written here is compiled into a real invocation, and every render of this component then dies on `Undefined variable $component`.

props.name: popover
props.comment: A trigger that opens a dialog with the calendar component, in place of the native field: the application's own calendar and date format, with the limits and options below. The native field keeps the browser's keyboard, picker and date wheel. A boolean, as on the color picker; the value, the field names and `wire:model` are the same in both forms.

props.name: clearable
props.comment: With `popover`: a button in the trigger that empties the field.

props.name: presets
props.comment: With `popover`, the calendar in the dialog; see the calendar component for each. `months` is 2 for a range and 1 for a single day unless given, and `presets` lists ranges beside it.

components.name: datetime-picker
components.description: A date and a time, picked from a calendar and a list of times in a dialog

props.name: value
props.comment: The moment, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, or a date object, read as the wall-clock time it names in the application's time zone. With `range`, two moments: `start/end`, an array with `start` and `end`, or a range object (Values\DateTimeRange).

props.name: range
props.comment: Two moments, a start and an end, each with its own time, taken together with Select.

props.name: placeholder
props.comment: What the trigger shows without a value.

props.name: help
props.comment: An explanation shown in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and part of the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: size
props.comment: The height of the trigger: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: type
props.comment: `button`, a trigger that shows the moment, or `input`, a field that takes the moment typed in segments in the locale's order, with a button that opens the dialog. Without `range`.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: Shows the moment and opens nothing.

props.name: clearable
props.comment: A button in the trigger that empties the field.

props.name: withConfirmation
props.comment: A day and a time wait for Select; Cancel, Escape or a press outside leave the value as it was.

props.name: defaultTime
props.comment: The time a day picked without one takes at once, `HH:MM`; with `range`, one for both ends or `HH:MM/HH:MM` for the start and the end.

props.name: time
props.comment: How the time is picked: `list`, from a list of times beside the calendar, or `input`, typed in segments below it with the list as suggestions. A typed time waits for Select.

props.name: interval
props.comment: The minutes between two times in the list.

props.name: timeFormat
props.comment: `auto` follows the locale, or `12-hour` and `24-hour`.

props.name: minTime
props.comment: The first and the last time of every day, `HH:MM`. A `maxTime` before the `minTime` runs over midnight and opens the night.

props.name: min
props.comment: The first and the last moment a reader can pick: a moment, a day, a date object, `today` or `now`. The calendar reads their days, the time list their times on those days.

props.name: unavailable
props.comment: Days, times and spans a reader cannot pick: `2026-10-24`, `12:00`, `12:00-13:00`, `2026-10-23T10:00`, `2026-10-23T15:00-16:00` or date objects, as a list or separated by commas.

props.name: openTo
props.comment: Where the dialog opens without a value: the calendar on its month, the time list at its time.

props.name: minRange
props.comment: With `range`: the fewest and the most days a range may cover, both ends counted, and the ranges such as "Last 7 days" beside the calendar (see the calendar component).

props.name: months
props.comment: The calendar inside the dialog: see the calendar component for each. `months` is 1, or 2 with `range`.

props.name: locale
props.comment: BCP-47 locale for the moment on the trigger, the calendar and the times, with the word between the day and the time. Null → the application locale. Its other texts stay in the application's language.

components.name: editor
components.description: Rich-text editor (ProseMirror-based peer-dependency adapter; Tiptap recommended) with toolbar + hidden-input form binding

props.name: required
props.comment: `required` — DECLARED rather than left to the attribute bag. Undeclared, Blade folded it into the bag and it landed on a wrapper div, where it is invalid HTML that nothing reads: no native constraint, no aria-required, no asterisk. StrictnessGate did not complain either, because `required` is in its HTML passthrough list — so it looked like a legitimate attribute all the way down. The result was a required field that submits empty, in the same form as a plain input that behaves correctly.

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call when you leave the editor. A refusal KEEPS what you wrote — see the note above. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: format
props.comment: html | json

props.name: extensions
props.comment: array of editor extension NAMES (hint for window.wirekitEditor)

props.name: engine
props.comment: The engine this field opens in, by name: its factory is `window.wirekitEditors[engine]`. An application with several schemas registers one factory per name, and a field that names its engine never takes another's, which after `wire:navigate` could be whichever bundle ran last. Without a name the field takes `window.wirekitEditor`.

props.name: toolbar
props.comment: false | 'basic' | 'full' | 'custom'

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Takes the editor out of use: the document stays in its field, dimmed and announced as unavailable (`aria-disabled` on the surface), nothing in it can be changed, and nothing is submitted. Built on the non-editable rendering (`editable` false): no toolbar, no form field, the engine mounted with `editable: false`. Declared rather than left to the attribute bag, where it lands on the wrapper div and nothing reads it.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: size
props.comment: sm | md | lg

props.name: maxHeight
props.comment: Cap the editable area's height (any CSS length, e.g. '20rem' / '50vh'). The content host already scrolls (overflow-y-auto); maxHeight gives it a CEILING so a long document scrolls INSIDE the field instead of growing the page downward. null = grow with content (the size's min-height is the only bound). Width is set the normal way — the editor is w-full, so constrain it with a class/style on the component (e.g. style="max-width: 40rem" or a max-w-* class).

props.name: commands
props.comment: Command vocabulary to render. '|' is a visual separator. Commands the active extension set doesn't support simply no-op (Tiptap's chain ignores them).

components.name: field
components.description: Form field wrapper with label, hint, and error

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label (partials/field-help).

props.name: announceError
props.comment: When true (default), the error message renders as an ARIA live region (aria-live="polite") so a validation error that appears dynamically — e.g. after a Livewire round-trip — is announced by screen readers without the focus having to return to the field. Set false when the surrounding page runs its own live region for form errors (avoids a double announcement). The aria-describedby link to the field is unaffected either way.

props.name: orientation
props.comment: vertical (label above) | horizontal (label beside)

props.name: name
props.comment: The error-bag key the group answers for, and every entry below it: a rejected entry of an array field is filed under its index. The fieldset keeps it as its name attribute.

props.name: error
props.comment: A message for the group as a whole. Takes precedence over the error bag.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: Render the group error as a polite live region. Precedence: this prop, then the surrounding form's announce-errors, then config('wirekit.a11y.announce_error').

props.name: help
props.comment: One explanation for the whole group: a question mark beside the legend, the same help a field shows beside its label, and the text as the group's description. The controls inside then need no help of their own. Read only where the set has a legend to stand beside.

props.name: helpField
props.comment: The name of the field the help explains, which its `wirekit:field-help` event carries. Without it the event names the group's `name`; a set that stands for one field and reads no error-bag key of its own names that field here.

props.name: asField
props.comment: The set stands for ONE field whose parts are its controls, such as a value in every language: the legend reads as a field's label, at a label's distance from the first control, and the hint or the error follows the controls, as under a field. A field beside the set then stands on the height of its first control.

props.name: required
props.comment: The group as a whole is required, such as a choice nobody may skip: an asterisk after the legend, as a required field draws after its label, and the word in the legend, which a screen reader reads on entering the group. No control in it takes the browser's own check.

components.name: file-upload
components.description: Drag-and-drop file upload area

props.name: required
props.comment: `required` — DECLARED rather than left to the attribute bag. Undeclared, Blade folded it into the bag and it landed on a wrapper div, where it is invalid HTML that nothing reads: no native constraint, no aria-required, no asterisk. StrictnessGate did not complain either, because `required` is in its HTML passthrough list — so it looked like a legitimate attribute all the way down. The result was a required field that submits empty, in the same form as a plain input that behaves correctly.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: uploadSeparately
props.comment: With `multiple` and `wire:model`, each file of a selection goes up in a request of its own, so one over a server's or a proxy's limit fails alone. Off by default: the property then updates once per file, and an `updated` hook runs once per file.

props.name: capture
props.comment: `capture` is its OWN attribute, not a token inside `accept`: `accept="image/*;capture=camera"` is a legacy Android spelling that no current browser reads and which sets a MIME filter no file matches. It cannot come from the caller's side either: this input takes named attributes and `wire:model*` only, never the whole bag, so a `capture` passed as a plain attribute would never reach the element.

props.name: variant
props.comment: Shape, not chrome. `default` is the full drop AREA — a block-level dashed rectangle that fills its container, which is right for a field in a form. `compact` is the same control at button height, shrink-to-fit, for a dense row beside badges and `size="sm"` buttons where a full-width area would push every neighbor onto its own line. Both keep the native input, the click-to-browse path and the drop handlers — only the shape differs.

props.name: label
props.comment: Null rather than the sentence itself, so the component can tell "the caller said nothing" from "the caller chose this text". The shipped default is written for a large area; in `compact` it would make the control wider than the row it exists to fit, so there it names the control without painting. Resolved below from the translation catalog: a literal default here would stay English whatever the application's language.

props.name: removeLabel
props.comment: Accessible name for each file's remove button. The `:name` placeholder is replaced with the file name at runtime, so translators control word order (some languages put the object before the verb). Overridable per call site.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

components.name: filter-builder
components.description: Active-filter chip bar with a typed add/edit popover (field/operator/value)

props.name: fields
props.comment: [{key,label,type,operators?,options?}]; type: text|number|select|date|bool

props.name: value
props.comment: active filters [{field,op,value}] (two-way via wire:model bridge)

props.name: name
props.comment: hidden-input name for plain-form submission

props.name: searchable
props.comment: free-text search box

props.name: searchDebounce
props.comment: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before announcing `search-change`. Same reasoning, same default and same escape as data-table's `searchDebounce`: this input dispatches straight to whatever the host wired the event to, and the documented wiring is a Livewire round trip. Without the wait that is one request per CHARACTER, and every answer but the last is discarded. 0 disables it.

components.name: form
components.description: Form wrapper that inherits an error-announcement policy to every control inside

props.name: announceErrors
props.comment: Error-announcement policy inherited by every WireKit form control nested inside this form. null  — inherit the global wirekit.a11y.announce_error config (the default) false — turn the per-control aria-live error region OFF for all controls inside. Use this when THIS form renders its OWN error summary — a role="alert" list that announces every message and pulls focus (the WCAG 3.3.1 pattern) — so the per-field live regions would otherwise double-announce. true  — force it ON for all controls inside. A per-control :announce-error still overrides this for that one control.

props.name: submitOnce
props.comment: After its first submission the form holds every further one back until the page changes, so a second press sends nothing. For a form Livewire does not send: `wire:submit` has its own loading state, and the script leaves a submission it took over alone.

props.name: submitOnceRelease
props.comment: How long a held form waits for the page to change, in milliseconds, before it takes a submission again: an answer that leaves the page as it is, such as a download. `0` waits for the page alone.

components.name: image-editor
components.description: A crop over an image, moved and sized by dragging its frame or handles, the arrow keys or number fields, held to a ratio when one is given

props.name: src
props.comment: The image to crop, its text alternative and its size in pixels. The size holds the crop to its ratio and its smallest side before the file arrives; without it the editor waits for the image's natural size.

props.name: value
props.comment: The crop to start with where no `wire:model` hands it over: `x`, `y`, `w` and `h` in percent of the image. None is the whole image, or with a ratio the largest crop of it, centered.

props.name: ratio
props.comment: The crop's width over its height in pixels, as `9/16`, `1/1` or `16/9`; null for a free crop.

props.name: min
props.comment: The crop's smallest side, in pixels of the image.

props.name: label
props.comment: The name of the crop, and the sentence that says how to move and size it.

components.name: image-hotspots-editor
components.description: Points on an image, set with a click or a button, moved by dragging, the arrow keys or number fields, and ordered in a list, for image-hotspots

props.name: src
props.comment: The image the points stand on, its text alternative and its size in pixels.

props.name: phoneSrc
props.comment: The phone's file. With it, a switch edits either image, and each point has a position of its own on the phone's, `phoneX` and `phoneY`.

props.name: value
props.comment: The points to start with where no `wire:model` hands them over: the list `image-hotspots` takes, each an array with `x` and `y` in percent and whatever else the page keeps on it.

props.name: label
props.comment: The name of the list of points, and the sentence that says how to edit them.

components.name: input
components.description: Text input with prefix/suffix support

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method this component should call, when it should show the new value before the server has agreed to it. A refusal keeps your value — see the note above. Null leaves the component exactly as it has always rendered. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: hideLabel
props.comment: render the label sr-only (kept for assistive tech) — for compact toolbar / header fields

props.name: formatHint
props.comment: For `type="date"` and `type="datetime-local"`: a sentence below the field when the browser writes dates in a different order than the page, with a worked example, as date-picker's prop of the same name. A native date field takes its order from the browser's language and never from the page, so `03.04.2026` and `04/03/2026` are both accepted and one of them is the wrong day. Nothing renders while the two orders agree. Other types ignore it.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: reserveMessage
props.comment: Keep the message line's height whether or not there is a message. props.comment: When true (default), the error message renders as an ARIA live region (aria-live="polite") so a validation error that appears dynamically — e.g. after a Livewire round-trip — is announced by screen readers without the focus having to return to the field. Set false when the surrounding page runs its own live region for form errors (avoids a double announcement). The aria-describedby link on the input is unaffected either way.

props.name: success
props.comment: Success / valid state. Pass a string to show a green confirmation message below the field (e.g. "Username available"), or `true` for just the green border with no message. `error` always wins when both are set.

props.name: mono
props.comment: Monospace the field value — for SKUs, measurements, codes, hashes. Swaps the input font to --font-wk-mono; off by default. The <x-slot:leading> / <x-slot:trailing> named slots put an icon or addon INSIDE the field frame (a search glyph, a unit) — distinct from the text-only `prefix`/`suffix` props.

props.name: clearable
props.comment: Optional trailing affordances (opt-in; off by default). `clearable` shows an X button that empties the field, refocuses it, and dispatches input/change so wire:model / x-model sync. `copyable` shows a copy-to-clipboard button with a brief "Copied" state. props.name: clearLabel
props.comment: What the X says it clears, as its accessible name and its tooltip. A field whose X lifts more than the text (a found receipt, a started return) says so here.

props.name: counter
props.comment: A count of the characters under the field, counted in the browser as they are typed, with no request to the server: `true` shows the number, "12 / 60" when the field has a maxlength; a string is the sentence that shows it, with :count, :max and :remaining.

props.name: tokens
props.comment: Tokens a button under the field puts into it, in the browser, without a request: at the caret the reader left there, or at the end. A list of tokens, or a map of each token to what it stands for, which a screen reader hears after it: `['{YYYY}' => 'the year']`.

props.name: required
props.comment: HTML5 form-state props — declared so the schema and AI / IDE tools know about them, and passed through like the bare HTML attributes (required, disabled, readonly) a plain form writes.

props.name: own
props.comment: A value derived from other fields, such as a code from a name, that a switch below the field opens for a value of the reader's own. `false` follows the derived value, read-only; `true` holds the reader's own. Unset, the field has no switch.

props.name: ownLabel

props.name: ownModel
props.comment: The Livewire property the switch writes, live, so the server derives the value again when it is turned off, and the lock follows without saving.

props.name: ownName
props.comment: The switch's name in a form without Livewire.

props.name: helpId

props.name: helpField

props.name: announceError

props.name: help

props.name: value

props.name: placement
props.comment: Where the options panel opens against the field: any placement `dropdown` takes. The panel still flips to the other side when the chosen one has no room.

props.name: panelWidth

props.name: truncated

components.name: otp-input
components.description: One-time password input with auto-focus

props.name: required
props.comment: `required` — DECLARED rather than left to the attribute bag. Undeclared, Blade folded it into the bag and it landed on a wrapper div, where it is invalid HTML that nothing reads: no native constraint, no aria-required, no asterisk. StrictnessGate did not complain either, because `required` is in its HTML passthrough list — so it looked like a legitimate attribute all the way down. The result was a required field that submits empty, in the same form as a plain input that behaves correctly.

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call when the code is COMPLETE — not per keystroke. A refusal keeps what was entered; see the note above. Null leaves the component exactly as it has always rendered. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: alphabet
props.comment: Which characters a box accepts. Defaults to digits. "OTP" does not mean "numeric": an ambiguity-free alphabet like ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789 (no I/1, no O/0) is chosen deliberately — it carries far more entropy per character and survives being read aloud. With digits only, such a code could not be entered at all: every keystroke outside the set is discarded, and the boxes stay empty with no message.

props.name: group
props.comment: How many boxes form a group. Null gives one wrapping row, breaking wherever the width runs out. Without it an eight-digit code can break 6+2 or 5+3 and a six-digit one 5+1, wherever the width runs out: a break in the middle of a code, at no boundary the code has, while somebody copying it from an email reads one line there. The prop does NOT force a break: the groups sit in a wrapping row and each group itself does not wrap, so a row that fits stays a row and a row that does not breaks at a group boundary. `group="4"` on eight digits is one row on a desktop and 4+4 on a phone.

props.name: justify
props.comment: Where the row of boxes sits inside the control's own width. A one-time code almost always stands in a centered card — the heading, the sentence and the button are all centered — and the row of boxes has to be able to follow. At `start` the container carries `flex flex-wrap` and no `justify`, so it packs to the start; and when the row wraps, the second line sits under the start of the first rather than under its middle. A prop rather than a note, because the call site cannot reach the row: a class written on the tag lands on the outer wrapper, so a centering utility there never touches it. The only other way is a rule over this component's internal markup — `justify-content` on a descendant `[role="group"]` — which breaks silently the day the markup moves. `start` by default, where a flex row packs when nothing tells it otherwise; `center` and `end` move the row, and `stretch` fills the control's width instead; see the alignment block below.

props.name: size
props.comment: The size of every box: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default), `lg` 48px, `xl` 56px. A touch device already lifts the boxes to the touch target, through the `pointer: coarse` floor in the stylesheet. What it cannot reach is a surface that is worked by finger and reports a FINE pointer — a till or a kiosk with a mouse plugged in, where the boxes stayed 40px. `lg` clears 44px on any pointer, and the class list below gives each size its own box so the square survives. `md` by default, so no existing field changes size.

props.name: autofocus
props.comment: Focus the first box on load. A one-time-code screen is single-purpose: the reader arrived from a redirect whose status region has already said the code was sent, and the boxes are the only thing on the page they came to operate. Every sibling screen in that flow focuses its field, and an `autofocus` written at the call site would land in the attribute bag and be dropped with it: one extra Tab for a keyboard reader, and a pre-filled email field read out first for a screen-reader reader. Default false, because an OTP field is not always alone on its page and moving focus on a page somebody is already reading takes them somewhere they did not ask to go. WCAG forbids neither; the call site knows which of the two screens it is building.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Disable the whole control: native `disabled` on every digit box and on the hidden input that carries the combined value, plus `aria-disabled` on the group so a reader who lands there before reaching a box hears it too. Declared here because the attribute bag never reaches the digit boxes: the only reads are `->only('class')` on the wrapper, `->whereStartsWith('wire:model')` on the hidden input and `->get('aria-label')`. Undeclared, a one-time-code field written `disabled` would emit nothing anywhere and stay fully typeable, pasteable and submittable, announced as editable, and the `disabled:` variants below could never fire.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: Read-only as a native field is: every box keeps its tab stop and the code is sent, and nothing changes it, not a key, a paste or a code the platform fills in. Declared for the reason `disabled` is: the attribute bag never reaches the boxes, and undeclared the attribute landed on the wrapper, where it is no valid attribute and stops nothing.

Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError

props.comment: Names the RECORD as well as the field. "Edit: Title" is useless in a list of twenty rows — a screen reader then reads twenty identical entries and the user cannot tell which one they are on.

props.name: trigger
props.comment: What the reader SEES. There is deliberately no `none`: plain text is not focusable, so a value with no button is unreachable by keyboard entirely (WCAG 2.1.1). `focus-only` gives the quiet look without that defect.

props.name: openOnValueClick
props.comment: Whether clicking the VALUE opens the editor. Separate axis from `trigger` — one is what you see, the other is what acts.

props.name: control
props.comment: Which control the editor renders.

props.name: options
props.comment: Options for control="select" — key => label.

props.name: displayValue
props.comment: What READ MODE shows when the stored value is not the readable one: a select stores a key, an amount stores 1299, a date stores an ISO string. Defaults to the value, and resolves itself for a select.

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: Read-mode text when there is no value. Deliberately NOT called `placeholder`: on input, textarea and select that name already means the HTML attribute, and a second `placeholder` meaning something else would damage the prop vocabulary rather than extend it.

props.name: commitOn
props.comment: `explicit` — only the confirm control commits. `blur` additionally commits when the control loses focus. Forced to explicit for a select, see below.

props.name: size
props.comment: sm / md / lg only: `md-compact` exists on input and select but not on textarea or number-input, so offering it here would throw for two of the four.

props.name: width
props.comment: Cross-axis behavior. `auto` measures the content, so the width DOES jump when the editor opens and that is the honest choice for a short value in running text. `full` takes the container width, and then read and edit boxes are the same width — which is the half of layout stability that can actually be promised.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Takes the field out of use: the value stays readable, dimmed, and neither the pencil nor the value opens the editor; the pencil is disabled and the control inside is disabled, so a surrounding form submits nothing of it. Declared rather than left to the attribute bag, where it lands on the wrapper div and nothing reads it.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: Read-only: the value stays readable and is not dimmed, and nothing opens the editor. There is no pencil, since editing is no action here. Undeclared, the attribute landed on the wrapper div, where it stops nothing.

props.name: loadingTarget
props.comment: NOTE: `loadingTarget`, not `target` — the same distinction the button draws, so a page using both does not have to remember two spellings.

props.name: rows
props.comment: Textarea height, forwarded to the textarea's own `rows`. `auto` is its content-sizing mode: the editor opens as tall as the text it replaces and grows while typing. A row count pins a fixed height instead, so a four-line value opens into a three-row box the reader has to scroll to see their own text in. Ignored for every control except `textarea`.

props.name: saveTimeout
props.comment: How long to wait for the developer's `wirekit:inline-edit-saved` / `-failed` answer before giving up, in milliseconds. 0 disables the bound and lets the editor stay busy indefinitely — only sensible when the answer is genuinely guaranteed.

props.name: unknownMessage
props.comment: What the reader is told when that bound is reached. Without it the live region would fall back to the EMPTY STRING and abandon the save in silence. A field that announced itself busy and then says nothing at all is the worst of the three possible outcomes — a screen-reader user is left with no way to know whether the edit was kept, and sighted readers only see a spinner stop.

props.name: help

props.name: reserveMessage
props.comment: Keep the message line's height whether or not there is a message. Wasted space in a stacked form, and the difference between a working toolbar and one that jumps in a horizontal row: an appearing error grows this element, and every sibling in the row re-anchors to the new bottom edge. props.name: success
props.comment: Success / valid state — string shows a green confirmation below, `true` shows just the green border. `error` always wins when both are set.

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: What the field says when there is nothing to choose: `options` is empty and no option arrives through the slot. A selection filled from records shows only its placeholder before the first record exists, and the reader learns neither what is missing nor where to create it. Set, the select is disabled while it is empty, and the sentence below it is its description. Unset, an empty select renders as it always has.

props.name: emptyHref
props.comment: Where the missing record is created. Renders a link after `empty-text`; leave it null for a reader who may not create one.

props.name: emptyAction
props.comment: The link's text. Name what it creates ("Add a supplier"); without it the link reads "Create one".

props.name: emptyNavigate
props.comment: Whether the link moves to that screen with Livewire's `wire:navigate`, as the other links of an application that changes screens without reloading do. A link to a fragment of the same page never takes it, since Livewire would fetch the page instead of scrolling to it.

props.name: value
props.comment: The pre-selected option. It has to be a declared prop: `<select>` has no `value` content attribute, so an undeclared one fell into the attribute bag and rendered onto the element, where HTML ignores it. `value="pro"` then selected nothing and the browser fell back to the first option — the field showed one choice while everything reading the component believed another.

components.name: slider
components.description: Single-thumb slider with value display

props.name: required
props.comment: `required` — DECLARED rather than left to the attribute bag. Undeclared, Blade folded it into the bag and it landed on a wrapper div, where it is invalid HTML that nothing reads: no native constraint, no aria-required, no asterisk. StrictnessGate did not complain either, because `required` is in its HTML passthrough list — so it looked like a legitimate attribute all the way down. The result was a required field that submits empty, in the same form as a plain input that behaves correctly.

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call when the slider should show the new value before the server has agreed to it. The value is sent when the gesture ends — see the note above. props.name: error
props.comment: `error` is declared like `label`: undeclared, `:error` on this control would land in the attribute bag and render as a stray HTML attribute — a validation message the developer wrote, silently not shown, on a control that is part of forms.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out — an app that runs its OWN error summary would otherwise double-announce here.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: valuePosition
props.comment: Where the shown value sits: `end`, beside the track as it always has, or `below`, on its own centered line under the track. `below` keeps every track of a form the same length: beside the track each slider reserves room for its own widest value, so five sliders with five different value words drew five different track lengths.

props.name: marks
props.comment: Step marks: a list of values (`[0, 25, 50, 75, 100]`) for plain ticks, or a value => label map (`[0 => 'Low', 100 => 'High']`) for labeled ticks.

props.name: valueTextMap
props.comment: Decouple the announced aria-valuetext from the visual tick labels: an explicit value => spoken-text map lets you show NUMERIC ticks but announce semantic meaning (e.g. [1 => 'Low', 5 => 'High']). Falls back to the `marks` labels.

props.name: tooltip
props.comment: Show a value bubble above the thumb that follows it as the user drags.

components.name: swatch-group
components.description: A choice of colors or patterns as swatches, one as radios or several as checkboxes

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: options
props.comment: The options, each an array: `value`, `label` (the name, which a color alone cannot say), and `color` or `image` as on a swatch. `available` false draws a line across the swatch and reads "unavailable" with the name, and the option stays a choice; `disabled` true takes it out of the choice. `lang` names the language of the label where it differs from the page's.

props.name: value
props.comment: The chosen value, or with `multiple` a list of them, for a form without `wire:model`.

props.name: multiple
props.comment: Several values at once, as checkboxes, as a filter takes them. Without it one value, as radios.

props.name: labels
props.comment: `hidden` keeps each name for assistive technology, `below` shows it under its swatch. A pill shows each name as its text, so neither changes it.

props.name: size
props.comment: The swatches' size and shape, as on a swatch: `pill` for values a name says best, such as sizes.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Disable every option.

props.name: required
props.comment: One value has to be chosen: the radios carry the native constraint and the group says so. With `multiple` the label carries the mark, and "at least one" is the application's rule.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: Read-only as a native field is: the tags stay on the page and are sent with the form, and nothing adds or removes one. Undeclared, the attribute landed on the frame, where it is no valid attribute and stops nothing.

props.name: counter

props.name: value

components.name: time-picker
components.description: Time selection input

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method this component should call, when it should show the new value before the server has agreed to it. Null leaves the component exactly as it has always rendered. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: format
props.comment: `24h` or `12h`. On the native field this is declared intent only: a native `<input type="time">` takes its 12-hour or 24-hour rendering from the browser and the operating system locale, and there is no HTML attribute that overrides it. It stays declared because it is a documented part of the surface and because an undeclared `format` would land on the control as a stray HTML attribute instead of being absorbed here. With `popover` it sets the clock the times are written on; unset, they follow the locale.

props.name: popover
props.comment: A trigger that opens a dialog with a list of times, in place of the native field: the application's own clock and language, every `step` from `min` to `max`. A boolean, as on the color picker; the value, the field's name and `wire:model` are the same in both forms.

props.name: time
props.comment: With `popover`: `list`, a dialog with the list of times, or `input`, the time typed in segments in the field, with the list as suggestions.

props.name: clearable
props.comment: With `popover` and the list: a button in the trigger that empties the field.

props.name: step
props.comment: The native `step` attribute, in seconds, exactly as HTML defines it: 900 is a quarter of an hour, 60 is one minute, null leaves the browser's own default of one minute. A value off the step is a step mismatch the form refuses to submit.

props.name: value
props.comment: Declared rather than left in the attribute bag, so that a date object arrives as itself: Blade casts a bound attribute that is not a prop to an escaped string before the template runs, and an Eloquent `datetime` cast would reach the control as `Y-m-d H:i:s`.

components.name: toggle
components.description: Toggle switch with label and hint

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method this toggle should call, when it should show the new state before the server has agreed to it. Null (the default) leaves the developer's own wire:model / wire:click untouched. It is a METHOD NAME rather than a boolean because the component cannot know the action otherwise — WireKit passes server actions through the attribute bag, so a component never sees the developer's wire:click. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out.

props.name: hideLabel
props.comment: Render the label sr-only (kept as the control's accessible name) — for a toggle in a table column or a toolbar whose surrounding chrome already names it. The <label> WRAPS the control, so the name is associated with the element rather than with the visible text and survives being taken off the screen. Mirrors input / select / textarea / combobox / checkbox `hideLabel`.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: onLabel
props.comment: The state in words beside the switch, such as "On" and "Off". Drawn from the checkbox itself, so the word follows the click before a server has answered, and hidden from a screen reader, which hears the switch announce its own state.

props.name: statePosition
props.comment: Where the words sit: `end` after the switch and its label, `start` before the switch.

props.name: onIntent
props.comment: The track's color for each state: `accent`, `success`, `danger` or `neutral`. On is the accent and off is neutral by default; "green on, red off" is `on-intent="success" off-intent="danger"`.

props.name: groupError
props.comment: Take the surrounding field.set's group error, or decline it. A control that belongs to the group but neither causes the rejection nor can resolve it says `:group-error="false"` and is then neither announced as invalid nor described by the group's message.

components.name: translatable-input
components.description: A value in several languages: the primary field, a chip with its state for each further language, one language at a time or all of them in columns

props.name: label
props.comment: The value's name: the legend over its languages, and the label of its field when there is one language.

props.name: locales
props.comment: The languages: a map of code to name (`['de' => 'Deutsch', 'en' => 'English']`), or a list of codes, which are named in the reader's language through `intl` and by their code without it.

props.name: primary
props.comment: The code of the primary language. The first of `locales` without it.

props.name: value
props.comment: The text per language, a map of code to text, for a form without `wire:model`.

props.name: name
props.comment: The base of the fields' names: `name[de]`, `name[en]`. Without it, a field bound with `wire:model="name"` is named `name.de`, the key its error is filed under.

props.name: multiline
props.comment: A `textarea` per language instead of an `input`.

props.name: rows
props.comment: The lines of each textarea, or `auto` to grow with its text.

props.name: inline
props.comment: How many further languages stand as fields without asking. With more, a chip opens its language, one at a time, and "Show all languages" opens all of them.

props.name: hints
props.comment: A short sentence for one language, under its field: a map of code to text, such as `['en' => 'Translated by machine']`. A code that is not in `locales` is left out.

props.name: error
props.comment: A message about the value as a whole. An error of one language stands at its own field.

props.name: required
props.comment: The primary language only: a translation stays optional.

props.name: placeholder
props.comment: The primary field's placeholder. A translation shows the primary text as its placeholder.

components.name: unsaved-hint
components.description: Says beside the save button that a form holds values its server does not have yet; x-wk-unsaved frames each unsaved field and can ask before leaving

props.name: text
props.comment: The sentence shown while a field in the scope is unsaved. The slot replaces it.

props.name: question
props.comment: What `x-wk-unsaved.confirm` asks before the reader leaves with unsaved fields, unless the scope names its own question in `data-wk-unsaved-confirm`. A browser asks a reload or a closed tab in its own words, so this is the question before a `wire:navigate` visit, asked in the dialog below.

components.name: toggle-button
components.description: Single two-state button that stays pressed (aria-pressed) — the bold/italic/mute shape

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call when the button should show its new pressed state before the server has agreed to it. A refusal puts the old state back — see the note above about the wrapper this adds. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: pressed
props.comment: The two-state truth. In the controlled default, bind it to your own state — the pressed state of a formatting control lives in the document, not in the button. It also seeds the initial state in self-toggle mode.

props.name: selfToggle
props.comment: Uncontrolled convenience. When true the button flips its OWN aria-pressed on click (Alpine), so it works standalone — a formatting toolbar, a docs demo — with no Livewire wiring. Default is controlled: a bare click must NOT flip it locally and drift from the document's truth.

props.name: size
props.comment: Visual weight, forwarded to the underlying button.

props.name: icon
props.comment: One glyph, the same in both states. The pressed surface carries the state, as it always has.

props.name: onIcon
props.comment: A glyph per state, swapped as the state changes. Both are needed: one alone would swap with nothing. The same alias works in every icon preset, where an outline and a filled variant of one glyph would not, so a second alias is how a state gets its own shape.

props.name: tooltip
props.comment: A hint shown on hover and focus. On a toggle with no visible label it is ALSO the accessible name, because a glyph is not a name and a hover never happens on a touch screen.

props.name: activeIntent
props.comment: The color of the icon while pressed: `accent` or one of the four status intents, with `primary` accepted as `accent`, the color it names everywhere else. Color is never the state on its own here: the surface changes either way.

props.name: onLabel
props.comment: A label per state, such as "Sound on" and "Sound off". A button whose label says its state is not a toggle in the ARIA sense, so it renders WITHOUT aria-pressed: announcing "Sound on, pressed" would say the state twice, and the APG button pattern rules the pairing out.

components.name: tool-call
components.description: One tool invocation an assistant made — name, status, arguments as JSON, and the result behind a disclosure

props.name: name
props.comment: What was called. This is the name a reader recognizes — `search_docs`, `get_weather` — and it names the arguments block and the settled announcement, so it is required in practice: a tool call nobody can name is a spinner with extra steps.

props.name: status
props.comment: Where the call stands: pending — queued, nothing has happened yet running — in flight (the block is aria-busy and the label shimmers) done    — returned, the result is in the slot failed  — returned an error, and the slot holds it

props.name: arguments
props.comment: The arguments the model passed, shown as JSON. An array is encoded here; a string is printed as given, so an application that already has the provider's raw JSON does not pay a decode/encode round trip to display it.

props.name: seconds
props.comment: Seconds the call took, for the settled label. The APPLICATION owns this number — it knows when the call started, and a stopwatch in the browser would disagree with it the moment the page re-renders from the server. Null keeps the plain status word.

props.name: open
props.comment: Whether the result opens closed. A finished call's result is reference material, so it is collapsed by default; a failure opens, because an error nobody sees is not reported.

components.name: app-rail
components.description: Full-height module rail with tooltip, below (captions under the icons), or inline labels

props.name: labels
props.comment: How an item names itself. tooltip — icon only; the label is the link's accessible name and appears on hover/focus in a tooltip. The narrowest form, and the default. below   — a caption under the icon. Wider, and it removes the hover dependency, which matters on touch where hover does not exist. inline  — the label beside the icon, in a wide rail. This is the shape a single-column application wants when the rail IS the navigation.

props.name: expandable
props.comment: Adds a toggle that widens the rail to `inline` labels and back, persisting the choice. Orthogonal to `labels`: the toggle switches between the width `labels` selects and the expanded width, so `labels="below"` plus `expandable` gives captions that become full labels.

props.name: expanded
props.comment: Initial state on a first visit, before storage answers. Left unset, the cookie driver below is allowed to answer it instead — which is the whole point of that driver, so an explicit value here wins and turns the seeding off.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.comment: The state on a FIRST visit, before the store has anything to say. It is the third case the persistence has always been missing: an explicit `expanded` wins and turns the seeding OFF, a stored value decides when there is one, and with neither the component fell back to a hard `false`. An application whose rail should start open and follow the reader afterwards could not say so — the nearest thing was rebuilding the kit's own cookie read in a layout, superglobal fallback and all. Both drivers answer this the same way, which is the half that makes it one idea rather than two. The cookie driver seeds the first RENDER from here; the local driver renders from here and then hands this same value to the store read as its fallback, so an empty localStorage keeps it instead of collapsing to `false`. Default `false`.

props.name: persist
props.comment: Storage key. Null keeps the choice for the session only.

props.name: persistDriver
props.comment: WHERE the choice is remembered: 'local' (default) or 'cookie'. No server can read localStorage, so a rail that remembers being expanded would render collapsed and widen itself after the first paint, moving the content column. A small nonced script after the column closes that gap: it reads the stored flag while the parser is still working and swaps the width class before anything is painted. The script carries `WireKit::cspNonce()`, the same answer `fonts.blade.php` gives for its inline <style>, so a strict `script-src 'self'` policy with a nonce runs it. Where a policy refuses it anyway, the column falls back to exactly the behavior described above. A cookie is the only store Blade and Alpine both read, so this driver mirrors the flag there and the first render is already right. Opt-in on purpose: writing a cookie where a developer asked for localStorage is a behavior change, and a cookie is something an application has to be able to account for.

props.name: tone
props.comment: The surface. Each tone re-points the `--color-wk-rail-*` roles in dist/wirekit.css; every class below reads only those, so a tone is a change of variables rather than a parallel set of utilities. Override the roles in your own CSS to reskin one tone, or the `:root` defaults to reskin them all.

props.name: variant
props.comment: Shape. `flush` is the edge-to-edge chrome column with a single inline-end edge. `panel` is the floating rounded strip that sits ON the page with a gap around it — the shape that pairs with the app-shell's own `panel` prop. (The component tag is deliberately NOT written here. Blade is a text preprocessor and does not know it is inside a PHP comment: an `x-wirekit::` tag in one gets COMPILED, and the compiled component construct lands in the middle of this array. The failure reads "unexpected token" at a line that has nothing to do with it.)

props.name: indicator
props.comment: How the current module is marked. `pill` fills the item's own box. `edge` draws a bar on the inline-end edge of the rail, pointing at the column it selects — which reads better when the rail is very narrow and a filled box would dominate.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the navigation landmark. A console shell has TWO <nav> landmarks side by side, and a screen-reader user moving between landmarks cannot tell them apart unless each says what it is. Passing aria-label or aria-labelledby directly wins over this default and suppresses it, so the element never carries two conflicting names.

props.name: trackCurrent
props.comment: Keep the current entry with the address in a rail Livewire keeps across `wire:navigate` visits with `@persist`, which it does not render again: after each visit the entry whose link matches the page takes the current state and `aria-current`, in the browser (`x-wk-current`, utils/current.js). `app-rail.item` reads it from here.

props.name: name
props.comment: The workspace's name. Drawn only where the rail is wide enough to read it; it stays the mark's accessible name in every mode regardless, so a narrow rail is not an unlabeled circle to a screen reader.

props.name: description
props.comment: A second, quieter line under the name — the plan, the environment, the role. Drawn only beside the name, never on its own: a subline without its subject says nothing.

props.name: href
props.comment: Makes the whole block a link. Leave it out for a switcher — wrap the component in a dropdown trigger instead, so the control is a button and announces itself as one.

props.name: scope
props.comment: There is a second mark slot, `expanded`, and it is not declared here because a named slot is not a prop. It is documented here because this is where a reader looks. A rail that opens has two widths, and a brand usually has two forms: a signet that fits in the narrow column, and a wordmark that is only legible in the wide one. Put the signet in the default slot and the wordmark in `<x-slot:expanded>`, and the two swap with the rail's LIVE state. Leave the slot out and the default slot is drawn at every width. The markers below are emitted only when there is something to swap with, so a rail with one mark carries no rule that could hide it. The accessible name comes from `name` and is unaffected, which is what makes the swap safe. Both forms are presentation: the hidden one is `display: none` and reaches no accessibility tree, while `name` stays in it at every width. A developer who instead labels the images themselves gets two names for one thing, and only one of them at a time — which is the trap this arrangement avoids rather than one it creates.

props.name: label
props.comment: An optional heading. It is drawn only where the rail draws labels at all — in the icon-only rail there is no room for it, and a section title that does not fit is worse than none — the labels themselves never truncate, so a heading there would wrap to three or four lines and push the modules off the screen. It stays the group's accessible name in every mode regardless, which is what lets a screen-reader user tell two clusters of icons apart.

props.name: separated
props.comment: A separator line above the group. The rails these come from cluster modules with a rule rather than a heading — a heading costs a row of height that a narrow column does not have. Off for the first group, which needs no line above it.

props.name: as
props.comment: `a` or `button`. A rail module is a destination, so a link is the default and stays the default — this exists for the OTHER thing a rail entry legitimately is: the trigger of a dropdown, which our own console-shell blueprint builds out of one. As a link that trigger is subtly broken: a link activates on Enter and not on Space, so Space would leave the menu closed and `aria-expanded` at "false". In a `viewport` shell Space is not even scrolling, so the key would have no effect anywhere. On top of that every click on an `href="#"` pushes a history entry and writes `…#` into the address bar, and a modified click opens a dead duplicate tab. Opt-in on purpose: switching automatically when `href` is "#" would be the tidier API, and would change the rendered element, and the caller's CSS with it, for a caller who never asked.

props.name: current
props.comment: What the active entry is to a screen reader: `page` for the page itself, the default, `location` for an entry that leads the section the page lies in, `true` for neither. The highlight is the same for all three.

props.name: icon
props.comment: The module's icon. A bare name string ("chart-bar") resolves through the WireKit icon system; a <x-slot:icon> or inline markup renders verbatim. Consistent with sidebar.item / dropdown.item / command-palette.item.

props.name: label
props.comment: The module's name. REQUIRED, and not merely by convention: in the rail's default mode nothing of it is drawn, so this string is the link's ONLY accessible name. Leave it out and a screen reader announces "link" — the failure that makes icon rails inaccessible in practice, and the reason this is a prop rather than the default slot (a slot cannot also be a tooltip's text without rendering twice).

props.name: truncate
props.comment: Opt-in: a visible name that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis instead of wrapping. This is a deliberate exception to an absolute rule, scoped to exactly what the rule protects. The rule below (a visible name is never truncated) is about destinations: "Insig…" cannot be told apart from "Insights" or "Insight reports", so a clipped module name names nothing. That argument does not reach an entry that is not a destination — the account trigger at the foot of a rail, labeled with a person's name, which is unambiguous even when cut and whose row would otherwise grow past its neighbors. So the default stays the rule. A caller who sets this takes the trade knowingly, on an entry where the name is not what tells the entries apart. The full name stays in the accessible name untouched (the span is clipped visually, never shortened), and it is repeated as a `title`, because the kit's own tooltip switches itself off while the rail is expanded and a clipped name would otherwise have no way back to its full text for a sighted reader.

props.name: badge
props.comment: A trailing counter. Digits where a label is visible, a dot where it is not — the digits have no room in a 3.5rem rail, but an unread signal must not simply vanish where it matters most. The count stays in the accessible name in BOTH states.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.comment: What the counter counts, as a sentence: "3 vouchers wait for review". A dot says only that something waits, and digits beside a visible name say how many but never of what. With it the module carries a tooltip with the sentence in every mode, under the name where the name is a tooltip as well, and the sentence becomes the link's description for a screen reader, so the bare count leaves the name. Ignored without a `badge`. A list of sentences names each waiting item on a line of its own: the tooltip shows at most `badgeLabelLimit` of them and then how many more there are, and the description names every one.

props.name: placement
props.comment: Where the tooltip opens. `right` is correct for a rail on the inline-start edge; a right-hand rail wants `left`.

props.name: shortcut
props.comment: The keyboard shortcut the module's tooltip draws after its name, ⌘ S on a Mac and Ctrl S elsewhere. Unset, the tooltip draws the one the module binds with `x-wk-shortcut`; this is for a shortcut registered another way, and `false` draws none.

components.name: app-shell
components.description: App shell with header, sidebar, and main content

props.name: viewport
props.comment: Viewport-fixer mode. Default (false) keeps a minimum of the viewport height, less any strip above the page — the shell grows with its content and the page scrolls as a document. When true, the root is pinned to the viewport height (100dvh, less any strip above the page) so the inner sidebar + main regions scroll INTERNALLY (brand pinned top, account menu pinned bottom) — the classic fixed-height admin-shell case. `dvh` (not `vh`) so the mobile browser toolbar collapse is handled.

props.name: sidebarInset
props.comment: Whether the in-flow sidebar column keeps its top and inline-start inset. True (default) is the card layout: the sidebar sits as a panel inside a padded column. False is the full-bleed navigation column — the sidebar meets the top and the inline-start edge of the shell with nothing between. A prop because the two utilities that produce the inset sit on the <aside>, and the attribute bag lands on the ROOT element — so as literals they would be unreachable from a call site by any means except a CSS rule targeting the vendor's own marker class and out-specifying Tailwind by emission order. Pair it with the sidebar's own `variant="flush"`: this removes the gap around the column, that removes the card inside it. (Named without its tag on purpose — a component tag written inside this comment block is compiled by Blade, not ignored, and takes the whole component down with a 500.)

props.name: headerPlacement
props.comment: Where the header slot renders. `shell` (default) spans the full width above the sidebar row. `content` puts it INSIDE the content column, so the sidebar runs the full height and the topbar begins beside it — the other common admin layout, without hiding the header slot at lg and hand-placing a topbar in the default slot. A `sticky` header stops working in this mode, and the reason is structural rather than a bug to fix here. `position: sticky` sticks to the nearest scrolling ancestor; in `content` mode the header's nearest one is the content column, which carries `overflow-hidden` (see the comment on that element below) and therefore never scrolls. Nothing sticks to a container that does not move. In `shell` mode the header is outside that column, so its scrolling ancestor is the page and sticky behaves as written. With `viewport` the question dissolves rather than being answered: the main region becomes the scroller and the header sits above it without moving at all, so it needs no sticky. Reaching for `sticky` there is harmless and does nothing. (The component tag for that region is deliberately NOT written here. Blade is a text preprocessor and does not know it is inside a PHP comment — an `x-wirekit::` tag in one gets COMPILED, and the compiled component construct lands in the middle of this array. The failure is "Undefined variable $component", which points at the render rather than at the sentence that caused it.)

props.name: panel
props.comment: The content column as an INSET rounded surface, floating on the shell's own background rather than meeting it edge to edge. The shape three of the reference consoles use: the chrome (rail, second column, top rule) is one surface and the content sits on it like a sheet, its inline-start corners rounded. lg only, and that is not a shortcut. Below the breakpoint the navigation is an off-canvas drawer and the content is the whole viewport — a rounded inset there would spend horizontal room a phone does not have on a decoration nothing is beside.

props.name: tone
props.comment: The shell's own chrome surface. `default` leaves the shell on --color-wk-bg. The other tones point the root at the same `--color-wk-rail-*` roles the rail and a toned sidebar read, so a shell, its rail and its second column become one continuous chrome surface with the content panel sitting on top of it.
