components.name: dropdown
components.description: Dropdown menu with items

props.name: name
props.comment: Pin the panel id across renders, as `alert-dialog`, `drawer` and `lightbox` allow too: it is what makes a Livewire round trip survivable from the call site.

props.name: block
props.comment: Fills the row it sits in instead of shrinking to its trigger. The wrapper is shrink-to-fit by default, which is right for a menu button in a toolbar and wrong for the one place a dropdown is the WHOLE row: the account trigger at the foot of a sidebar column. There the trigger's highlight has to span the row like the navigation entries above it, and no width set on the trigger can reach past a wrapper sized to that same trigger. A class from the call site cannot do this either — the wrapper's own `display` would have to be overridden, and two conflicting utilities resolve by stylesheet order rather than by which one the caller wrote.

props.name: label
props.comment: The menu's accessible name, handed to the panel the quick form composes. That panel is written by this file, not by the caller, so nothing on the call site can reach it except a prop of the parent — without this one, a quick-form menu could not be named at all. In the explicit form the caller writes the panel and gives it `label` there; the note above the panel's @props says why there is no generic fallback.

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method to call when the item is toggled, showing the new checked state before the server agrees. A refusal puts the old state back. Adds a `display: contents` wrapper — see the note above for why that is safe inside a menu. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: shortcut
props.comment: keyboard-shortcut hint at the inline-end

props.name: label
props.comment: The heading over the group's entries, which also names the group: "Account" over its pages.

props.name: shortcut
props.comment: keyboard-shortcut hint shown at the inline-end (e.g. "⌘K"), or a list of its keys

props.name: badge
props.comment: A count or a short word at the end of the entry, drawn as the sidebar item draws its badge, and part of the entry's name: "My drafts 3". Empty draws nothing.

props.name: active
props.comment: "This is the page you are on." A navigation menu's most common state. Without it the only mark on screen would be the focus ring the menu puts on its first item when it opens, which reads as a selection to everyone who did not put it there. Deliberately NOT painted as a background. Hover and focus already use the subtle surface, and a third thing that looks like those two would not tell them apart. The current entry is marked by weight and text color, which survives beside either.

props.name: role
props.comment: The ARIA role, `menuitem` unless a caller asks for something else. A group of MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE menu options is `menuitemradio` + `aria-checked` under the APG menu pattern, and no amount of `aria-current` substitutes: `aria-current` says which item is the current one within a set of related items and carries no group membership at all. A reader hears "System, current" instead of "System, radio button, checked, 1 of 3" — never told that the three are one choice, nor how many there are. Opt-in rather than inferred, because this sub-component cannot see whether its siblings form a set. The caller knows; the item does not.

props.name: label
props.comment: The menu's accessible name. See the note above @props for why it is a prop, and why an absent one stays absent.

props.name: model
props.comment: name of the Alpine variable holding the group's selected value

props.name: value
props.comment: this option's value

props.name: label
props.comment: Parent item text (or pass a <x-slot:label> for rich content)

props.name: icon
props.comment: Optional leading icon (WireKit icon system)

props.name: placement
props.comment: Floating UI placement of the child panel

props.name: offset
props.comment: Gap between the parent item and the child panel

props.name: ariaLabelFallback
props.comment: Optional fallback aria-label used when the trigger has no accessible name (icon-only triggers, responsive layouts that hide the visible label below sm). Defaults to "Open menu". Explicit aria-label / aria-labelledby on the inner button or an sr-only span both win over this fallback — see x-init below.

components.name: fab
components.description: Floating action button that fans out into secondary actions

props.name: label
props.comment: What the trigger does. REQUIRED in spirit: the trigger is an icon, so without this it announces as "button" and nothing else.

props.name: position
props.comment: Where it floats. 'end' is the inline-end corner — it follows the writing direction rather than assuming everyone reads left-to-right.

props.name: label
props.comment: What this action does. The button is an icon, so this is its whole name.

props.name: hideLabel
props.comment: Drop the label from the SCREEN while keeping it as the accessible name — the plain icon-only speed dial. Same meaning the prop carries on checkbox, so the name is reused rather than reinvented.

props.name: label
props.comment: The accessible name when the button carries no words of its own. Null rather than the default string, so the component can tell "the caller said nothing" from "the caller asked for this" — a distinction the name resolution below needs and could not otherwise make. The default is applied there.

props.name: position
props.comment: Where it floats — the inline corner, following the writing direction.

props.name: placement
props.comment: Which block edge it sits on. `block-end` (the default) is the canonical bottom-corner FAB and is unchanged; `block-start` moves it to the top.

props.name: haspopup
props.comment: What the button opens, so assistive tech announces it correctly. A single-action FAB is NOT a menu. Not given, a button opens a dialog (the canonical use is a feedback / compose modal) and a link with `href` navigates, so it announces nothing. Pass 'dialog' / 'menu' / 'listbox' / 'grid' / 'tree' as needed, or a falsy value to omit aria-haspopup entirely (a plain action that fires an event rather than opening a popup).

props.name: href
props.comment: Render an <a> instead of a <button> when the action is a navigation.

props.name: icon
props.comment: Optional icon name (resolved via the WireKit icon system). A slot overrides it.

components.name: hover-card
components.description: Content preview on hover

components.name: lightbox
components.description: Focus-trapped media viewer for images, video, and embeds — reusable, keyboard-navigable, event-driven

props.name: name
props.comment: Instance identifier. Any control can open this lightbox by dispatching `wirekit-lightbox-open` with a matching `name` + `index`.

props.name: items
props.comment: The slides. Each item is an array: ['src' => …, 'alt' => …, 'caption' => …, 'type' => 'image'|'video'|'embed'] plus 'altLang' and 'captionLang', the language of either text where it differs from the page's. `type` defaults to 'image'. A plain string is treated as a decorative image src.

props.name: loop
props.comment: Whether prev/next wraps around at the ends (true) or stops (false).

props.name: lockScroll
props.comment: Whether opening locks the page's scroll and makes the page behind inert. False for a viewer that lives inside a page region, such as a preview, where the page around it has to keep scrolling.

props.name: showCaptions
props.comment: Show each item's caption inside the lightbox.

props.name: overlay
props.comment: Backdrop color / opacity for THIS instance (any CSS color). Null → the themeable --color-wk-overlay-media token, the darker backdrop for media.

props.name: slideOverlay
props.comment: Per-slide overlay render-callback: a closure `fn($slide, $i)` returning markup to lay OVER the media of slide #$i in the viewer (a label, a watermark, a report control), shown only while that slide is. The wrapper is pointer-events-none; interactive controls inside opt back in with `pointer-events-auto`. Return a view or HtmlString for HTML (a plain string is escaped). Null → no overlay.

props.name: zoomable
props.comment: Zoom inside an open image: three buttons, the keys `+` `-` `0`, the wheel, a double click or a double tap, a pinch, and dragging the enlarged image. Images only; a video or an embed keeps its own controls.

props.name: maxZoom
props.comment: The largest scale, as a multiple of the size the image is fitted to. A number above 1.

components.name: mockup
components.description: Frame chrome for a screenshot or live composition — browser, window, code, phone, tablet

props.name: variant
props.comment: browser — URL bar + traffic lights (a web app screenshot) window  — title bar + traffic lights (a desktop app) code    — filename tab + traffic lights (a snippet, pairs with code-block) phone   — a phone frame tablet  — a tablet frame

props.name: url
props.comment: Shown in the browser variant's address bar.

props.name: title
props.comment: Shown in the window / code variant's title area.

components.name: modal
components.description: Dialog overlay with backdrop

props.name: confirmDiscard
props.comment: Whether the reader is asked before closing the dialog by Escape, a click beside it or its close button while its fields hold changes. On by default: a click beside a filled form would otherwise throw away what has been typed into it. A close the page makes and a Cancel control never ask. `discardQuestion` replaces the question, which is in the reader's language otherwise.

props.name: confirmShortcut
props.comment: Whether ⌘↵ or Ctrl+Enter presses the dialog's primary control while it is open, from a field as well. A modal has no confirm of its own: the control a page marks with `data-wk-dialog-primary` is the one, and without a mark nothing is pressed.

props.name: lockScroll
props.comment: Whether opening locks the page's scroll. False for an overlay that lives inside a page region, such as a preview, where the page around it has to keep scrolling.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.comment: Names the dialog when it has no header sub-component. A dialog with no accessible name is announced as just "dialog", and the failure is silent — see the aria-labelledby block below. (No component tag in this comment: Blade compiles tags inside comments too, and one here breaks the @props array it sits in.)

props.name: dismiss
props.comment: A Cancel: closes as a dismissal and announces it with `via: 'cancel'`, where the default closes the way a finished action does and announces nothing.

props.name: intent
props.comment: The look of the button the trigger draws, handed to it as written: a trigger above a list is usually `intent="neutral" surface="outline"`. Null keeps the button's own default. A trigger with `href` is a link, which takes `size` and has no intent or surface.

components.name: popover
components.description: Contextual content popover

props.name: label
props.comment: The panel's accessible name. It is a `role="dialog"`, so a screen reader announces this on entry — and the default said "Popover", which names the mechanism rather than the content. A page with two of them announced the same word twice.

props.name: padded
props.comment: Whether the panel pads its own contents. `false` hands the whole surface to the caller, which is what a panel with its own header, scroll region and footer needs: those three have to reach the panel's edges, and padding on the outside puts a gutter between the scrollbar and the border and stops a sticky header from sitting flush.

components.name: shortcuts
components.description: Keyboard shortcuts for a whole application — bound with x-wk-shortcut on the element they act on, by area, listed on ?, with a switch for single keys

props.name: singleKeys
props.comment: The application's stored choice for single-key shortcuts: true, false, or null for the choice this browser remembers. The switch announces each change as `wirekit:shortcuts-single-keys-changed` with `{ enabled }`, so the application can keep it with the person and render the next page with it.

props.name: heading
props.comment: The dialog's heading, "Keyboard shortcuts" in the reader's language by default.

props.name: level
props.comment: The level of the area headings inside the dialog ("Everywhere", "On this page"). The level is the caller's: 2 by default, so an area reads as a section of the dialog its title names.

props.name: intent
props.comment: The look of the button, handed to it as written. Null keeps the button's own default.

components.name: toast-region
components.description: Toast notification container

props.name: name
props.comment: scoped name — when set, listens on 'wirekit-toast-{name}' instead of global

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the stack, and the switch that makes it a LANDMARK. `role="region"` plus a name is a landmark, and this component is designed to be mounted several times on one page — one per corner, or one per section through `eventScope`. With a built-in name every one of them would be the same rotor entry called "Notifications", which is what axe reports as `landmark-unique`: the name meant to tell them apart would make them identical. So the role waits for a name the CALLER chose, never one the component can invent. Nothing is lost without it — the two live regions below are the announcement path, and they do not depend on the landmark. Name it after the surface ("Form notifications").

props.name: filled
props.comment: when true, toast uses full variant background color (like callout)

props.name: scope
props.comment: class-personalization scope — passed to WireKit::resolveClasses

props.name: eventScope
props.comment: CSS selector for DOM-containment event filtering

components.name: tooltip
components.description: Hover tooltip with configurable position

props.name: focusableTrigger
props.comment: Whether the trigger is a tab stop of its own, so a tooltip on something that is not a control (an icon, a word) is reachable by keyboard and not by hover alone (WCAG 2.1.1). `null`, the default, reads the slot: a slot that already holds a control is the stop a reader lands on, and its focus reaches the trigger and shows the tooltip, so the trigger stays out of the tab order rather than becoming a second stop with no name. `true` and `false` from the caller are kept as they are.

props.name: describes
props.comment: `false` when the tooltip text is ALSO the trigger's accessible name, as on an icon-only control named by its tooltip. Describing a control with its own name makes a screen reader say it twice ("Fast mode, button, Fast mode"), so the pairing is left out. Where that name is in the slot, as its words or its `aria-label`, the component leaves the pairing out by itself; this is for a name it cannot read there, such as one given through `aria-labelledby` or bound by Alpine.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Switch the tooltip off without removing it. A tooltip on a control that has become inert — a collapsed sidebar item, a disabled action — has to be able to go quiet, and `pointer-events-none` on the root is NOT a way to do that however much it looks like one: `mouseenter` is delivered to every ancestor of the element actually hit, whatever their own pointer-events value, so the handler fires and the panel appears over something that is supposed to be dead. Rendered as an attribute rather than passed into the factory, so a call site can bind it — `x-bind:data-wk-tooltip-disabled="collapsed"` — and get a tooltip that follows live state. The component reads it at trigger time.

props.name: surface
props.comment: The panel's surface. `inverted` is the classic tooltip, the text color as the background and the page color as the text, so it stands out on either theme. `elevated` takes the surface menus and popovers use: the elevated background, the body text and the theme's border.

props.name: shortcut
props.comment: A keyboard shortcut drawn after the text, as the `kbd` component draws its `shortcut`: ⌘ S on a Mac and Ctrl S elsewhere, named in the reader's language. Unset, the tooltip draws the shortcut the control in its slot carries in `x-wk-shortcut`; `false` draws none. A single-key shortcut is drawn only while single keys work.

props.name: as
props.comment:
What the host AND the trigger wrapper root in. `div` is the default; `as="span"` is what makes this component usable inside a text-level one. It has to move BOTH elements, and that is the whole reason it is one prop rather than two. A `
` inside a `

` is invalid HTML, so the parser closes the paragraph and hoists the div out — the trigger stops being a child of its text node and becomes its SIBLING. In a grid that sibling gets a cell of its own, which is how a warning glyph ends up next to the wrong row. Nothing about that is red: the Blade reads correctly, both markers are in the output so every assertion passes, and there is no overflow and no console error for a screen sweep to catch. The panel is unaffected either way — it lives in a `

components.name: tour
components.description: Guided product tour with steps

props.name: index
props.comment: When null (default), the index is auto-assigned via TourStepCounter::next() based on document order under the enclosing tour parent. Explicit :index="N" bypasses the auto-assignment — useful when steps render conditionally and the developer needs control over the numbering.

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 3 — a step's title inside the tour dialog — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

props.name: title
props.comment: The step's title, as a prop or as the `title` slot; the slot wins when both are given.

components.name: announcement-banner
components.description: Dismissible page-edge announcement bar with persisted dismissal and an optional inline CTA

props.name: position
props.comment: Where the bar lives. Sticky is opt-in — a bar that follows the reader is a stronger claim on the viewport than most announcements deserve.

props.name: strip
props.comment: A strip ABOVE the page: pinned to the top of the viewport, one line tall, never dismissible — for the line that says "this is staging", which has to be visible on every screen and must not change the application underneath it. It sets `--wk-strip-inset` on :root, and every surface that pins itself to the top of the viewport or takes the viewport's height folds that in — `app-shell viewport` gives the strip its height back, sticky page bars stick BELOW it. So the application moves down by exactly the strip and changes nothing else, whichever shell it uses. One line on purpose, and it is what makes "changes nothing" true from the first frame. A strip whose height a script had to measure would let the page jump once it ran. A fixed height lets the stylesheet know it before anything paints. Text that does not fit is cut on screen and stays whole in the accessible name; an announcement that needs several lines belongs in an ordinary banner, which flows with the page.

props.name: intent
props.comment: Semantic tint. `promo` is the marketing default (accent), the state intents carry the usual meaning.

props.name: surface
props.comment: How strongly the intent is applied: `soft` tints the bar (what it has always done), `solid` fills it with the intent's color and its own contrast-paired text. The same two treatments `badge` has, with the same names — a strip saying "staging" wants `solid`.

props.name: hue
props.comment: A HUE instead of an intent, 0-360: `250` is blue, `300` violet. For the environment line, where the color identifies the instance rather than a state — `warning` on staging would read as a warning about something that is not one. Independent of the theme's accent, which is monochrome by default, so `intent="info"` is not blue out of the box. Lightness and chroma come from `--wk-banner-hue-l` / `--wk-banner-hue-c`, chosen to keep AA against the text at every hue. The hue itself can also come from the stylesheet — `.env-staging { --wk-banner-hue: 300 }` — which survives a Content-Security-Policy that strips inline styles; without either, it follows `--theme-hue` where a preset sets one.

props.name: dismissKey
props.comment: A stable key makes the dismissal STICK across page loads. Without one the bar is not dismissible unless `persist` is explicitly turned off (below) — a close button that silently forgets is worse than no close button, so forgetfulness has to be a deliberate choice, never an accident.

props.name: persist
props.comment: Whether a dismissal is remembered across page loads (localStorage). On by default. Turn it OFF for a session-scoped notice that should reappear next visit — and it is what makes a live demo resettable, since a re-mount then brings the bar back instead of reading a stored "dismissed" flag.

props.name: dismissible
props.comment: Whether a close button exists at all, stated rather than derived. Left null, it is derived as it always was — and that derivation has a trap: `persist="false"` WITHOUT a key makes a bar dismissible (session-only), so a developer turning persistence off to be safe gets a close button they never asked for. `false` means never, whatever the other two props say. A strip is never dismissible regardless.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the region — and the LANDMARK waits for it. No default name, because one would make every banner the same landmark. `position` validates against top and bottom, so a page with a promo bar above and a notice below is a first-class composition, and a shared default would give it two `role="region"` landmarks both called "Announcement" that somebody paging through landmarks cannot tell apart. A component may not invent the name that turns itself into a landmark, so the role is gated on `filled()`, as in its siblings. Null, so the role is gated on the CALLER having supplied a name rather than on this file being able to invent one. The dismiss button still gets a composed name below, because a control needs one whether or not the banner is a landmark.

components.name: cta
components.description: Call-to-action banner section

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation when the CTA scrolls into view. Null = no animation (default — CTA renders without an entrance reveal).

props.name: size
props.comment: `size` — vertical-rhythm tier (mirrors hero's prop). One of `sm` / `md` / `lg`. Default `md` (= `--space-wk-section-md` at sm+ viewports). Mobile viewport (< sm breakpoint) drops one tier so the cta never overshoots vertical-padding budget on small screens.

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 2 — a call to action, usually a section of its own — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

props.name: title
props.comment: The heading and the text under it, as props or as the `title` and `description` slots; a slot wins when both are given, and a text that carries markup has to be the slot.

components.name: faq
components.description: FAQ block — accordion of questions that emits FAQPage JSON-LD derived from what it rendered

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the question list.

props.name: variant
props.comment: Visual treatment, passed through to the underlying accordion. 'flush' is the default here (not 'bordered'): an FAQ almost always sits inline in page content, where outer chrome only competes with the section around it.

props.name: level
props.comment: The heading level of the questions, 1 to 6, passed to every question as `variant` and `size` are. An FAQ right under the page's h1 takes 2, one under an h3 takes 4.

props.name: multiple
props.comment: Let several answers stand open at once. Default is one at a time, which is how people read an FAQ: they are hunting one answer, not comparing. A boolean rather than the accordion's `mode` string on purpose. `mode` is a forbidden prop name for new components — the house convention froze the shared-axis names, and the handful of components still on `mode` are grandfathered pending a migration. Widening that list for a brand-new component would be the wrong side of a rule that exists to stop exactly this drift. A bare boolean attribute also reads better at the call site than a string enum with two values.

props.name: schema
props.comment: Emit FAQPage JSON-LD for the questions rendered here. Turn it OFF when the same questions already appear elsewhere on the page, or when this FAQ is one of several: a page must carry exactly one FAQPage, and two of them compete rather than combine.

props.name: plainText
props.comment: Strip markup from the SCHEMA answer text (the visible answer is untouched). The schema is read outside the page, where the data-* attributes, Alpine directives and utility classes of nested components mean nothing, and plain text is what every reader of it takes reliably. The schema text stays DERIVED from what is rendered — same content, markup removed — so it cannot drift from the page.

props.name: findable
props.comment: Passed to the accordion: a question's answer stays findable by the browser's find in page.

props.name: animate
props.comment: Passed to the accordion: whether an answer animates its height open and shut.

components.name: faq-item
components.description: One question and answer inside an FAQ; records itself for the FAQPage schema

props.name: question
props.comment: The question. Rendered as the accordion trigger AND recorded for the FAQPage schema — one string, both jobs, so they cannot disagree.

props.name: questionLang
props.comment: The language of `question` where it differs from the page's, written on the question alone. The structured data keeps the text as it is.

props.name: schemaAnswer
props.comment: Escape hatch for the rare case where the schema answer must differ from the visible one in CONTENT, not just markup. Prefer `plain-text` on the faq: a hand-written duplicate is copy that can drift away from what the reader sees, which is exactly what deriving the schema from the render prevents.

props.name: open
props.comment: Starts open, rendered open by the accordion item. In single mode the first open question stays open. Unset, it follows the accordion item's default, which applies with `multiple` only.

components.name: feature
components.description: Individual feature card for feature grids

props.name: intent
props.comment: The canonical color axis, the one button, badge, progress, alert and callout all spell: primary | neutral | info | success | warning | danger. `tone` below is its back-compat alias and keeps working unchanged.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation when the feature card scrolls into view. Null = no animation (default).

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 3 — a card in a grid of features — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

components.name: feature-grid
components.description: Responsive grid for feature cards

props.name: scale
props.comment: Which spacing ladder `gap` names a rung on: `space` (the default) or the tighter `gap` ladder, as on `grid`.

props.name: stagger
props.comment: Cascade entrance animations across direct children. null = no stagger (default — each child animates simultaneously) true = enable with default 75ms step int  = explicit ms step (e.g. 125)

components.name: footer
components.description: Landing page footer with columns and legal

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation when the footer scrolls into view. Null = no animation (default — footer renders without an entrance reveal).

props.name: max
props.comment: `max` — container max-width tier for the inner content wrappers (columns, brand+legal row, default slot). Defaults to `xl` (= 80 rem). Same enum as the container primitive (sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/ full) so the footer aligns with the rest of the page chrome on the same vertical content-edge spine.

components.name: hero
components.description: Landing page hero with title, lede, and actions

props.name: asideWidth
props.comment: Only valid when layout="balanced". Tunes the copy:aside ratio from the default 50/50 to one of: 1/3 | 2/5 | 3/5 | 2/3. Under any non-balanced layout this prop is reported through the strictness gate and has no effect on the columns.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation. Null = no animation (default).

props.name: size
props.comment: `size` — vertical-rhythm tier. One of `sm` / `md` / `lg`. Default `lg` (= `--space-wk-section-lg` at `sm+` viewports). Mobile viewport (< sm breakpoint) automatically drops one tier — `lg` becomes `md` (= 5rem each side) so the bottom-empty-area-with-gradient class of bug (variant="dark" hero with gradient overlay produces a visually empty dark band below the content on narrow viewports when the section padding is too generous) doesn't recur. Pass `size="sm"` for the tightest spacing across every viewport.

props.name: tightOnMobile
props.comment: `tightOnMobile` — when true, drop an ADDITIONAL tier on mobile viewports for `size="lg"` heroes. Useful for dark-variant heroes with gradient overlays where even 5 rem of mobile bottom padding reads as a visible dead-zone below the content on 390 px-wide viewports (iPhone 12-class). Opt-in (default `false`) — does NOT change the rendering of any existing hero. For `size="sm"` and `size="md"`, the prop is a no-op (mobile already runs at the tightest tier).

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 1 — the page's main heading — the level a hero usually carries — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

props.name: fit
props.comment: Shrinks the title down to a floor so it takes the fewest lines the floor needs: true for the `--text-wk-fit-floor` token, a length such as `0.75em` for a floor of its own, null or false for none.

props.name: eyebrow
props.comment: The small text above the title and the title, as props or as the `eyebrow` and `title` slots; a slot wins when both are given, and a text that carries markup has to be the slot.

components.name: accordion
components.description: Collapsible content panels

props.name: variant
props.comment: Visual treatment of the container + items: - 'bordered'  → outer border + rounded card + row dividers + elevated bg (default). - 'flush'     → no outer chrome, just hair-line row dividers — for an FAQ that sits inline in page content. - 'separated' → each item is its own standalone card with a gap between them (the container draws nothing; items carry the chrome).

props.name: size
props.comment: Row density. 'md' is the default trigger/panel padding; 'lg' is roomier (larger padding + trigger text) for marketing / spacious layouts.

props.name: findable
props.comment: Closed panels stay findable by the browser's find in page, which opens the one a match lands in. Only where the engine supports it; elsewhere a closed panel is hidden. Read by every item through @aware.

props.name: animate
props.comment: Whether a panel animates its height open and shut. Read by every item through @aware. On by default. `x-wk-findable` carries a `.collapse` modifier that animates the height, reads `--transition-wk-duration` off the element, and skips itself under reduced motion, and `collapsible`, the sibling disclosure in this library, calls it too, so a page showing both eases both. A switch defaulting to OFF would have closed the ticket without changing the screen it came from. The escape hatch is here for a caller who wants the jump back, which is the half that makes the default safe to move.

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level each item's trigger is wrapped in (1–6). Defaults to 3, which is what every accordion shipped before this prop existed. The ARIA authoring practices require the level to be "appropriate for the information architecture of the page", and that is a property of the PAGE, not of the widget: an accordion sitting directly under the page <h1> wants level 2, one inside an <h2> section wants 3, and a fixed <h3> produces a skipped or flattened outline in every other position. Screen-reader heading navigation is where that shows up, so nothing on screen reports it. Items read this through @aware — the level belongs to the group, not to one row.

props.name: titleLang
props.comment: The language of `title` where it differs from the page's, written on the title alone, so the panel keeps the page's language.

props.name: open
props.comment: Starts open, and is rendered open, so nothing moves when the script starts. In single mode the first item with `open` is the one that stays open. Unset, it follows `components.accordion.item.open` in multiple mode; in single mode, where one panel is open at a time, a default cannot say which, so only an item that names `open` starts open.

components.name: action-bar
components.description: Floating action bar for bulk operations

components.name: activity-row
components.description: Activity-feed / timeline row with kind-colored dot, actor, timestamp, and badge slot

props.name: kind
props.comment: Activity kind — drives the leading dot color. The built-in set is commit / merge / deploy / comment / system / user; extend or recolor via `config('wirekit.components.activity-row.kinds')`. Unknown kinds fall back to the muted dot (no error — the map is intentionally open).

props.name: kindLabel
props.comment: What a screen reader hears for the kind, in place of the dot's color. The six built-in kinds are announced from the translation catalog; any other kind is announced by its key unless this names it.

props.name: actor
props.comment: Optional actor name, rendered bold at the start of the line.

props.name: timestamp
props.comment: Optional relative timestamp ("2 hours ago"), right-aligned + muted.

components.name: alert
components.description: Contextual alert message

props.name: variant
props.comment: back-compat alias of `intent`

props.name: intent
props.comment: canonical color axis: primary | neutral | info | success | warning | danger. null → falls back to `variant`

props.name: level
props.comment: The title as a heading of this level, 1 to 6: a reader moving from heading to heading finds it, and the headings in the text count from it. It keeps the alert's own size and line height. Null keeps the title a `div`, out of the page's outline; an unknown level is reported and keeps the `div` too, rather than placing the title at a level nobody chose.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation. Null = no animation (default).

components.name: attachment
components.description: File/image attachment card with formatted size, type label, upload state, and actions

props.name: name
props.comment: File name. Also the accessible name of the card.

props.name: bytes
props.comment: Raw byte count — formatted for display ("2.4 MB"). Pass the raw number; formatting is ours, so developers never hand-roll it.

props.name: type
props.comment: MIME type (e.g. "application/pdf"). Rendered as a short label ("PDF").

props.name: thumbnail
props.comment: Image source for a visual preview. Given → the media tile shows the thumbnail instead of the file glyph.

props.name: state
props.comment: Lifecycle: idle | uploading | done | error.

props.name: progress
props.comment: 0–100 while uploading. Drives the progress bar.

props.name: href
props.comment: Makes the whole card a link (download / open).

props.name: icon
props.comment: Override the media glyph with any icon name from the active preset.

props.name: animate
props.comment: Animate the upload progress bar while `state="uploading"` — a shimmer sweep that reads as "actively uploading". Opt-in (off by default), gated by prefers-reduced-motion at the CSS layer.

components.name: attachment-group
components.description: Group of attachments — vertical stack or horizontal scroll-snap row

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the group (e.g. "3 attachments").

props.name: orientation
props.comment: 'row' scroll-snaps horizontally (chat bubbles, tight rows); 'stack' lists them vertically (mail, detail panels).

components.name: assistant-message
components.description: AI assistant turn — roles, streaming body, model chip, reasoning disclosure, and coalesced screen-reader announcements

props.name: role
props.comment: Who is speaking: assistant (left, avatar + model chip), user (right), system (centered, muted — a configuration/system turn, not a person).

props.name: name
props.comment: Display name for the speaker. Null uses the role's own wording.

props.name: avatar
props.comment: Optional avatar image for the speaker.

props.name: model
props.comment: Model / engine chip (e.g. "atlas-2"). Assistant turns only.

props.name: intent
props.comment: Optional state tint on the bubble — for a turn that IS a state: an error answer (danger), a caution (warning), a confirmation (success), a note (info). neutral (default) keeps the plain role surface. Mirrors the message component's intent tint (bg + border at low alpha; the body text stays regular, never a state color).

props.name: streaming
props.comment: True while tokens are still landing. Marks the turn aria-busy and shows the streaming affordance.

props.name: citations
props.comment: The sources this answer cites, as numbered chips under the body. Takes whatever the retrieval layer produced: titles, arrays with label/href/snippet, or the application's own models — `CitationList` normalizes all three and drops an entry with no label, because a chip a screen reader announces as nothing is worse than no chip.

props.name: reasoningSeconds
props.comment: Seconds the model spent reasoning, for the disclosure's summary once the stream has ended: "Thought for 12s". The APPLICATION owns that number — it knows when the stream started, and a stopwatch in the browser would disagree with it the moment the page re-renders from the server. Null keeps the plain label.

props.name: announce
props.comment: How streamed output reaches assistive technology: sentence — flush each finished sentence (default; the readable choice) all      — flush once, when streaming stops off      — never announce (you narrate it yourself)

components.name: avatar
components.description: User avatar with image, initials, or status

props.name: fromInitials
props.comment: When true (with `initials` set and no `src`), derive a deterministic background color from the initials hash so the same person always gets the same color — replaces per-app crc32-palette helpers. The palette pairs an AA-contrast background with white text and is theme-independent. See Pushery\WireKit\Support\AvatarPalette.

props.name: statusVariant
props.comment: How to visually render the status: 'dot'  — small colored dot in the bottom-right corner (default). 'ring' — full colored ring that surrounds the avatar, separated from the image by a thin gap in the elevated surface color. The more prominent of the two: presence reads at a glance in a dense roster, where a corner dot needs looking for. Ignored when `status` is null.

props.name: remaining
props.comment: Optional overflow counter. When set, a trailing "+N" chip is rendered after the avatars (e.g. show 3 avatars + `:remaining="7"` → "+7"). The developer controls how many avatars they place in the slot.

props.name: size
props.comment: Sizes the overflow chip to match the avatars in the slot — set it to the same size you pass to those avatars.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the group as a whole (e.g. "5 collaborators"). The individual avatars keep their own alt text.

components.name: badge
components.description: Small status label

props.name: surface
props.comment: Surface treatment within the chosen intent: 'soft'    — tinted background + intent text (default; back-compat — the lifted chip with the themeable inset ring depth). 'solid'   — filled intent background + on-color foreground text. 'outline' — transparent background + intent ring + intent text.

props.name: tooltip
props.comment: Discoverable tooltip — surfaces the status explanation through WireKit's own tooltip component (hover / focus / touch / keyboard, aria-describedby) instead of the browser's native title attribute. The text is the badge label; the tooltip is the supplementary explanation (e.g. "Build failed" on a "Failed" badge).

props.name: leadingIcon
props.comment: Optional leading status glyph (icon alias, e.g. 'check' / 'clock' / 'x-circle' / 'shield-check'). Rendered decoratively before the label — the text is the accessible name, so the icon is aria-hidden.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.comment: Optional trailing glyph — mirror of leadingIcon, rendered after the label (e.g. an external-link arrow on a link badge). Also decorative.

props.name: dismissible
props.comment: When true, renders a trailing close button that removes the badge (Alpine x-show) and dispatches a `wirekit:badge-dismissed` event. Keyboard- and screen-reader-operable; label set via dismissLabel. A dismissible badge also emits data-replayable="true" so the docs preview frame offers a "↻ Replay" reset (inert in a developer app — no replay-button is injected there).

props.name: dismissLabel
props.comment: Null, not the English word: the fallback is resolved through the catalog in the block below. A literal default here is a label a translated application cannot reach — the dialog cancel button shipped that way, rendering an English control inside a fully translated German dialog while the catalog that would have fixed it was already installed.

props.name: wrap
props.comment: Multi-line mode. A badge is a fixed-height single-line pill by default. Set `wrap` for a long label that must break across lines: the fixed height is swapped for `min-h-*` + vertical padding so the pill GROWS with the text instead of the second line spilling below the surface.

props.name: truncate
props.comment: Keeps the pill on one line and cuts a long label at `--size-wk-badge-max` with an ellipsis. The whole label shows in a tooltip while, and only while, it is cut; with `tooltip` it leads that tooltip's panel instead, so one panel says both.

components.name: branch-switcher
components.description: Steps between several generated answers — prev/next, a live count, and a polite announcement per move

props.name: count
props.comment: How many variants there are. Required in practice: a switcher that does not know its own count cannot say "2 of 3", and the count is what the reader navigates by.

props.name: current
props.comment: Which one is showing, 1-based, because that is what the label says and what a caller reasons about. Out of range is clamped rather than refused — a server that regenerates and re-renders can legitimately hand over an index that no longer exists.

props.name: label
props.comment: Names the group for assistive technology. A switcher with no name is announced as a group of nothing, so an unset label falls back to a translated default.

props.name: loop
props.comment: Whether the ends wrap. Off by default: a reader stepping through variants expects the last one to be the last one, and silent wrap-around loses that.

components.name: bulk-selection
components.description: Row selection for a server list of its own: a header checkbox for the page, and every match on all pages offered with its count

props.name: total
props.comment: The number of matches on all pages. Without it, or when the page holds every match, the block offers nothing beyond the page.

props.name: filter
props.comment: Anything that names the filter the rows answer: a search text, a status, a key built from both. A render with another value while every match is selected clears that state and says so.

props.name: label
props.comment: The checkbox's accessible name. "Select all rows on this page" in the reader's language without one.

components.name: button
components.description: Action button with variants and loading state

props.name: wrapLabel
props.comment: Let a label that a USER typed take a second line. Default false: a label the application wrote belongs on one line, and a button that wraps mid-word is the defect there.

props.name: touchTextFloor
props.comment: On a touch screen, lift the label to the text floor the form fields lift to. Default false: a button on its own is right at its designed size; this is for one that shares a row with a field, where it would otherwise read a size below the field beside it.

props.name: touchFloor
props.comment: On a touch screen, stand at the touch target's size rather than at the drawn size with a hit area around it. Default false: in a dense toolbar an icon square grown to 44px runs over its container, so it keeps its size there and answers the finger through the area. This is for an icon button in a row with labeled buttons, which stand at 44px there.

props.name: iconOnly
props.comment: Show the icon alone and keep the label as the accessible name. The icon itself goes into `<x-slot:iconLeft>` or `<x-slot:iconRight>`. What this adds: a button carrying only an icon would otherwise take the HORIZONTAL padding of a text button and render as a wide box with a small glyph floating in the middle, and nothing would hold the label in the accessibility tree once it is hidden. The case is a row action that has to narrow on a phone, where a translated label can take half of what the table leaves. Without the prop the icon and an `sr-only` label go into the slot by hand and the padding is redone from outside; `clipboard-button` has the same shape. The label stays in the default slot. It is rendered visually-hidden rather than dropped, so the button keeps a real accessible name that is translated by the same `__()` the visible one went through and is reachable by voice control — which an `aria-label` on a control with no visible text is not, reliably. A caller who prefers `aria-label` can still use it; this only means they do not HAVE to.

props.name: iconOnlyBelow
props.comment: The same idea on an axis: show the label where there is room for it and the glyph alone where there is not. Takes a breakpoint NAME and measures the VIEWPORT. Viewport names only, and the difference is not cosmetic. `table.th hideBelowContainer` takes names from Tailwind's container scale, which runs from `3xs` to `7xl`; the viewport scale stops at `2xl`, which is why `table.th hideBelow`, the viewport half, takes `sm` to `2xl`. This prop takes those plus `xs`, written as the width it stands for (see the class table below). A name past `2xl` would emit a `max-3xl:` class that Tailwind generates nowhere, and nothing at runtime would notice: an unknown class is valid HTML and the button simply keeps its label. The viewport, said out loud, because the sibling prop measures something else. `table.th hideBelowContainer` measures a container the kit NAMES (`@container/wk-table`) precisely so an `@`-variant cannot be silently retargeted by whatever a caller nested it in. A button has no container of its own and sits anywhere, so a container-relative variant here would have to measure "the nearest one, whichever that is" — which is the ambiguity that naming was introduced to remove. A call site that really wants the container question writes the two `@`-variants itself and knows which container it set. `iconOnly` wins if both are given, and it says so rather than silently dropping one: asking for "always the glyph" and "the glyph below lg" together is a contradiction, not a refinement.

props.name: loadingTarget
props.comment: Scope the loading spinner + disable to THIS button's own Livewire action, e.g. loading-target="redeliver". The spinner is a child <svg wire:loading> with no target of its own, so Livewire falls back to hasActionForComponent() and flashes it on EVERY commit — including wire:poll refreshes and unrelated sibling actions. Setting loadingTarget emits wire:target so the spinner only reacts to that action. NOTE: this is `loadingTarget`, NOT `target` — a `target` prop would collide with the HTML target attribute (target="_blank" + the rel tabnabbing auto-inject). Null = the untargeted behavior; scoping is strictly opt-in.

props.name: disableOnLoading
props.comment: Whether the busy state DISABLES the control, or only marks it busy. `disabled`, the default, costs the focus: the browser blurs a control the moment it becomes disabled, so the element the reader just activated stops being focused for the whole in-flight window and focus falls to `<body>`. That is WCAG 2.4.3, on every request. `false` swaps the attribute for `aria-busy`, which tells assistive technology the control is busy while it stays focusable and in the tab order. Neither attribute announces the wait. Livewire's `.attr` sets the attribute to `true` (its `toggleBooleanStateDirective` does), so this yields a valid `aria-busy="true"` rather than the attribute's own name. The default is `true`, and the trade is the developer's to make: a control that stays enabled while its action is in flight can be pressed twice.

props.name: orientation
props.comment: 'horizontal' (default) joins children left-to-right; 'vertical' stacks them. Literal default (a sub-component, so it does not dotted-read its own config — mirrors avatar.group / accordion.item).

props.name: stackBelow
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl — below that width the group stacks: it joins on the block axis instead of the inline one, so a row whose labels fit on a desktop does not run off a phone. Only meaningful on a horizontal group; a vertical one already stacks at every width.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the group (e.g. "View mode"). Recommended when the group acts as a single control (segmented toggle, pagination cluster).

components.name: sign-in-button
components.description: A button that signs in with Google, Apple, Facebook, PayPal or Amazon, drawn by each service's guidelines with the logo the application provides

props.name: service
props.comment: The service: `google`, `apple`, `facebook`, `paypal` or `amazon`, or `passkey` for the browser's own sign-in with a passkey.

props.name: href
props.comment: Where the sign-in with the service starts, the route that redirects to it. Without it the component is a button, for a `wire:click` of the application's own.

props.name: action
props.comment: What the button offers: `continue` ("Continue with Google"), `sign-in` or `sign-up`. Meta and PayPal name no words for signing up, so there it continues.

props.name: variant
props.comment: The look within what the service allows, its first by default. Google: `auto`, `light`, `dark`, `neutral`. Apple: `auto`, `black`, `white`, `outline`. Facebook: `white`, `blue`. PayPal: `blue`, `gray`. `auto` follows the page's mode. Amazon's image is its only look.

props.name: logo
props.comment: The service's logo, a URL. Unset, `wirekit.sign_in.logos.<service>` from the config. For Amazon, the whole button image. Apple's logo takes the color of the button's words, so it can be given as `['white' => …, 'black' => …]`, and an image as one file per pixel density, `['1x' => …, '2x' => …]`.

props.name: label
props.comment: The words on the button, in place of the ones `action` gives.

props.name: pill
props.comment: A pill instead of the kit's corners, a shape Google and PayPal offer.

props.name: block
props.comment: As wide as its container, the way a sign-in page stacks them. `false` keeps it as wide as its words.

components.name: button-group
components.description: Welds adjacent controls into one unit — collapsed inner radii and a single seam, RTL-safe

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the group ("Text alignment", "Save options").

props.name: orientation
props.comment: horizontal (default) welds left-to-right; vertical welds top-to-bottom.

components.name: calendar
components.description: Calendar date display

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: Livewire method to call optimistically. The date appears selected immediately and is put back if the call fails. Absent -> the component renders without an optimistic layer. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: range
props.comment: Multi-month display — render N consecutive months side by side (1 = the classic single grid). Clamped 1..4 in the Alpine component. Two-click range selection. `value` then reads and writes `YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD`, the spelling the date-picker's own range flag already uses — a value moved between the two keeps its meaning. Written WITHOUT the component tag on purpose: Blade compiles component tags across the whole file before a PHP comment means anything, so naming one here compiles it, and the failure arrives as `Undefined variable $component` from a line that is not code.

props.name: selectableHeader
props.comment: Replace the static month label with native month + year <select> jump controls for fast navigation. Opt-in; off by default.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.comment: First day of the week: 0 (Sun) .. 6 (Sat), Monday by default, which matches the event-calendar default. Configurable via config/wirekit.php; `null` there, or `locale` here, follows the application's locale (Support\LocalizedDate::firstDayOfWeek()).

props.name: locale
props.comment: BCP-47 locale for every date the calendar writes: the month heading, the weekday columns, the names of the days and the first day of a week that follows the locale. Null → the application locale. Its texts stay in the application's language.

props.name: required
props.comment: A required calendar stops an empty submit, as a native required field does; see the stand-in below. Declared, so it does not land on the root, where it would do nothing.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Locked as a disabled field is: no day, arrow, preset or header control can be pressed, and the form receives none of the calendar's fields.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: Shown as a read-only field is: the months and days can be read and moved between, nothing picks a day or a preset, and the form still receives the value. `disabled` wins over it.

props.name: min
props.comment: The first and the last day a reader can pick: a day, a date and time, a date object, `today` or `now`, each read as its day in the application's time zone (Support\CalendarLimits).

props.name: unavailable
props.comment: Days a reader cannot pick: a list, or days separated by commas.

props.name: minRange
props.comment: The fewest and the most days a range may cover, both ends counted. Range mode only.

props.name: presets
props.comment: With `range`, a list of ranges beside the calendar: the keys Support\DatePresets names, `today`, `last7Days`, `thisMonth` and the others, as a list or separated by spaces, and `custom` for a range picked in the grid; `true` for the default list. A range outside the limits stays in the list and cannot be picked. Not with `optimistic`, whose layer takes one day at a time.

props.name: withToday
props.comment: A button beside the arrows that goes back to today's month, and picks today there.

props.name: weekNumbers
props.comment: A column with the ISO 8601 number of each week.

props.name: fixedWeeks
props.comment: Six weeks in every month, so that the calendar keeps its height from month to month.

props.name: openTo
props.comment: The month the calendar opens on without a value: a day, `YYYY-MM` or a date object.

props.name: size
props.comment: The size of the day cells: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: flush
props.comment: Without the panel's frame: no border, shadow, background or padding, for a calendar placed on a surface of its own, as the datetime picker places it in its popover.

components.name: callout
components.description: Highlighted information callout

props.name: variant
props.comment: back-compat alias of `intent`

props.name: intent
props.comment: canonical color axis: primary | neutral | info | success | warning | danger. null → falls back to `variant`

props.name: stripe
props.comment: Opt-in one-sided accent stripe (default OFF). The plain callout is the alert-style 4-sided tinted border; a one-sided colored stripe reads as generic dashboard chrome, so it is not the default. Pass `stripe` to add the accent bar deliberately.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation. Null = no animation (default).

props.name: title
props.comment: The heading, as a prop or as the `title` slot (the slot wins when both are given). It was a slot only, and `title="…"` on the tag then landed on the wrapper as an HTML attribute: a tooltip, with no heading drawn. `alert` takes it both ways, and so does this.

props.name: level
props.comment: The title as a heading of this level, 1 to 6: a reader moving from heading to heading finds it, and the headings in the text count from it. It keeps the callout's own size and line height. Null keeps the title a `div`, out of the page's outline; an unknown level is reported and keeps the `div` too, rather than placing the title at a level nobody chose.

components.name: card
components.description: Content container card with optional link

props.name: surface
props.comment: The canonical surface axis, spelled as on button: outline | elevated | flat. `variant` below is its back-compat alias and keeps working unchanged.

props.name: intent
props.comment: The color role of the border: neutral (the default) | info | success | warning | danger, in the tones `callout` draws its own border in, so a card around a warning callout can carry the same border. Only the border takes it; background and shadow stay those of the surface.

props.name: chevron
props.comment: Say at rest that the card leads somewhere: a chevron at the inline end. The pointer cursor and the hover shadow are the only other signs, and a phone shows neither, so there a card with `href` looked exactly like one with nothing behind it. Opt-in, because drawing it by default would change the layout of every clickable card that already exists. Read only on a card that links or runs an action.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation when card scrolls into view. One of 11 base presets (or any -in / -out variant). Null = no animation (default).

props.name: overflow
props.comment: What the card does with a child that reaches past its box. The default clips, which is what makes the rounded corners cut the content inside them — but it also clips a badge pinned to a corner, an avatar that scales on hover, or a focus ring that extends past the edge. `visible` releases all of it. A prop rather than an !important utility override on the base class, because that override is not the same thing: it removes the corner clipping for EVERY child, and nothing says so until someone drops a full-bleed image or a table into that card.

props.name: collapsible
props.comment: Fold the card under its own head: the head becomes the trigger, and everything in the slot, body and footer, folds away beneath it. Without it the card has no head, no region and no script of its own.

props.name: open
props.comment: Start a collapsible card open. A fold the reader made on an earlier visit never closes it on load, so a card that needs the reader is open every time. Read when the card first renders: during the visit the state is the reader's. Null unless given: a card that does not fold hands an `open` it was given to its element, as `as="details"` needs.

props.name: openWhen
props.comment: The reasons a collapsible card stands open for, as the server sees them now: a list of names, or a map of each name to whether it holds. With one the card starts open, and after a response only a reason it did not have opens it again, so a card the reader folded stays folded.

props.name: persist
props.comment: A key under which the browser remembers whether the reader left the card open. An application that keeps this in its own store passes it as `open` and saves `wirekit:card-toggled` instead.

props.name: name
props.comment: The name `wirekit:card-open` opens the card by, reported in `wirekit:card-toggled` as well. Handed to the element on a card that does not fold, as `open` is.

props.name: heading
props.comment: The text of a collapsible card's trigger. The `heading` slot takes markup instead.

props.name: level
props.comment: The level of the heading the trigger stands in, 2 to 6.

props.name: description
props.comment: The line under the heading, shown whether the card is open or closed. The `description` slot takes markup instead.

props.name: findable
props.comment: Closed content stays findable by the browser's find in page, which opens the card. Switch it off for content that must stay out of sight until the reader opens it.

props.name: padded
props.comment: Comfortable padding by default. Set padded=false for edge-to-edge content (a flush hero image, a full-bleed table). When false, the body also tags itself so a raw <table> dropped inside still gets readable cell padding (see the .wk-card-body[data-wk-padded="false"] rule in dist/wirekit.css).

props.name: description
props.comment: A sentence under the heading. A `description` slot takes markup.

components.name: carousel
components.description: Image/content carousel with autoplay

props.name: orientation
props.comment: horizontal (default) | vertical

props.name: perView
props.comment: How many slides share the view. '1' is the classic one-up carousel; the rest show neighbors, which is what a product row or a logo rail wants. Only meaningful horizontally — a vertical carousel is one slide tall.

props.name: label
props.comment: What this carousel is FOR. A carousel of testimonials is not an image carousel, and the name is the first thing a screen reader reads.

props.name: label
props.comment: The slide's accessible name. `role="group"` conformance does not require one, but `aria-roledescription` is what makes a screen reader say "slide" instead of "group" — and it is unreliable on an element that has no name at all, so a track of unnamed slides reads as N identical groups with nothing to tell them apart. It is a PROP rather than only an `aria-label` passthrough because a prop is what the props parser, the JSON export and the api-map can see; an attribute that happens to work is not a documented affordance, and the parent's own name for the same idea is `label` too. Deliberately NOT defaulted. There is no honest built-in name here: an anonymous Blade slide has no index of its own, so anything this file could invent would name every slide identically — the same reasoning that gates `role="region"` on a caller-supplied name everywhere else in this library, rather than on a name the component made up.

components.name: cart-item
components.description: Ecommerce cart line — thumbnail, name, unit price with compare-at, quantity stepper, line total, remove control

props.name: name
props.comment: The product name. Also the thing the remove control has to say, which is why it is a prop rather than a slot: ten controls that all announce "Remove" cannot be told apart by anyone using voice control, and a slot cannot be read into an aria-label.

props.name: href
props.comment: The name as a link to its product, in either layout. The controls of the line still say the name in theirs.

props.name: nameLang
props.comment: The language of the name, where it is not the page's, such as a product sold under its name in another language. It goes on the name alone, so a screen reader says it in that voice.

props.name: image
props.comment: Thumbnail. `imageAlt` defaults to empty on purpose — the name is already in the row as text, so a repeated alt reads the product twice. Pass one only when the image carries information the name does not.

props.name: price
props.comment: Unit price, and the struck-through previous price. Both go straight through to `price`, which already draws the strike AND an sr-only "Previous price" — this component does not re-solve that, and must not.

props.name: maxPrecision
props.comment: At most this many decimals for the unit price and the previous one, handed to their `price`: a piece can cost 0.045 €. The line total is an amount and keeps its currency's digits.

props.name: locale
props.comment: The locale the row writes its numbers in: every amount, handed to each `price` with the currency, and the quantity. Unset, they follow the application's locale, as a `price` of its own would.

props.name: lineTotal
props.comment: What the line costs at this quantity. The APPLICATION computes it. A cart that multiplies here would own state, and cart state belongs to Livewire rather than to this library — every second application has to take an assumption like that back out.

props.name: quantity
props.comment: The quantity column. `min` defaults to 1 because a cart line with zero of something is a removal rather than a quantity, and `max` is the stock ceiling when the caller knows it.

props.name: size
props.comment: The size of the stepper. `lg` rather than the `md` default, and that is a deliberate choice: `--size-wk-md` is 2.5rem = 40px, which clears WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24px, level AA) with room but misses the 44px of SC 2.5.5 (level AAA) and of platform touch guidance. `--size-wk-lg` is 3rem = 48px and clears both. Raising the token instead would move every component that reads it for one ecommerce case, so the preset carries it and a caller can still override.

props.name: unit
props.comment: A unit suffix for the stepper — "kg", "pair", "m". `number-input` already has `suffix`.

props.name: quantityName
props.comment: The name a form sends the quantity under, for a cart that works without script: `lines[42][quantity]`. Without one the field carries no name, because a field named after its id would be sent under a name the page never chose and no application could match to a line.

props.name: removable
props.comment: Whether the built-in remove control renders. The `remove` slot overrides it entirely.

props.name: removeIcon
props.comment: The glyph of the built-in remove control, an icon alias of the preset: `close` draws a cross, `trash` a bin. A − that takes the line out (`removesAtZero`) draws it too, so a line says "remove" with one picture.

props.name: readonly
props.comment: A line that is only shown, never operated: the customer-facing screen of a till, a receipt, an order confirmation. The quantity reads as text with its unit instead of a stepper, which on a screen nobody touches would look operable and do nothing, and the built-in remove control goes. A `remove` slot still renders: writing one is the caller's decision.

props.name: hideQuantity
props.comment: A read-only line without its quantity, visibly and for a screen reader: an article whose quantity another device shows, such as the weight a scale displays, where a "1" would read as one piece or one kilogram. An editable line ignores it: its field is its quantity.

props.name: unitPrice
props.comment: The unit price a measured article has to show beside its price, the Grundpreis of the German PAngV: "10,00 € / 1 pair". Handed to `price`, which formats it and puts it where price-marking law wants it; `unitMeasure` is the reference, "kg" or "1 pair".

props.name: layout
props.comment: `compact` sets the line in two rows for a narrow column, a till's for one: the name on one line beside the line total, and under them the variant and the unit price on the left, the quantity and the line's actions on the right. `default` is the row a shop's cart shows.

props.name: stepper
props.comment: `buttons` shows − and + with the quantity between them, and each press dispatches an event for the application to act on: `wirekit:cart-decrement` or `wirekit:cart-increment`, with the line's key. Every press counts, and the quantity shown is the one the application answers with. `field` is the number field a `wire:model` binds.

props.name: removesAtZero
props.comment: Whether the application takes the line out when its quantity reaches zero. With `stepper="buttons"` and `:min="0"`, the − whose press brings the line to zero then draws the remove glyph and is named "Remove", because that is what the press does. It still dispatches `wirekit:cart-decrement`: the application decides what the press means.

props.name: totalSize
props.comment: The size of the line total, on the scale of `price`: `xs` to `xl`. A screen read across a counter looks for what a line costs first, and at the default size the total stands no larger than the name. Without it the total takes the size `price` is configured with.

props.name: fitTotal
props.comment: Shrinks the line total down to a floor so it fits its line, as `fit` on `price`: true for the `--text-wk-fit-floor` token, a length for a floor of its own, null or false for none. In the compact line the name keeps eight characters before the total shrinks, and gives up more only once the total stands at its floor.

components.name: cart-list
components.description: Semantic list that holds cart lines — names the list for assistive tech and draws the separators between them

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the list. A cart is usually one of several lists on a checkout page, and a `<ul>` with no name is announced as "list, 3 items" beside every other one — the name is what tells them apart.

props.name: divided
props.comment: Whether to draw a separator between lines. `divide-y` compiles to a border-BOTTOM on `:not(:last-child)`, so the rule belongs to the list rather than to the line: a line cannot know whether it is the last one, and CSS has no previous-sibling combinator to tell it. `cart-item` therefore ships spacing and no border, and the two must stay that way — a border on both would double.

components.name: cart-summary
components.description: Order totals panel — subtotal, discount, shipping, tax and an emphasized grand total above the rule

props.name: subtotal
props.comment: The amounts. ALL of them come from the application, and none is derived here — the same rule `cart-item` follows for `lineTotal`, and for the same reason: totals are where tax rules, tiered pricing, gift cards and currency rounding live, and a library that guessed at them would be wrong in every second shop.

props.name: shipping
props.comment: `null` hides the row entirely. `0` renders as "Free" rather than as a zero amount, which is the one piece of interpretation this component does and the reason it is written here rather than left implicit: a shop that would rather show 0.00 passes `shippingNote`.

props.name: discount
props.comment: A reduction. Rendered as a negative amount, because a positive number beside the word "Discount" reads as an addition to anyone scanning the column.

props.name: currency
props.comment: Forwarded straight to `price`, which owns every formatting decision in this package.

props.name: locale
props.comment: The locale every amount is written in, handed to each `price` with the currency. Unset, an amount follows the application's locale, as a `price` of its own would.

props.name: shippingNote
props.comment: Replaces the shipping AMOUNT with a phrase — "Calculated at checkout", "Free over €50". Wins over `shipping` when both are given, because a shop that says both means the words.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the panel. It is a `<section>` with a name rather than a bare box, so a reader can reach the totals directly instead of arrowing through every cart line.

props.name: level
props.comment: The heading level is the CALLER's, not this component's. A cart page whose outline already has an <h2> above the summary needs an <h3> here, and a component that writes its tag literally forces a broken outline on it. Default 2: the summary under the page's <h1>.

components.name: chat-marker
components.description: In-thread meta row — streaming/tool status, system note, or labeled date break between chat messages

props.name: variant
props.comment: default    — a centered inline status / system note row border     — the same row with a hairline under it (row boundaries) separator  — a centered label flanked by rules (a date break)

props.name: icon
props.comment: Optional leading glyph (decorative — the row text carries the meaning).

props.name: status
props.comment: Renders the row as a live region so a text swap inside it is ANNOUNCED. Use for streaming / progress rows ("Thinking…", "Explored 4 files").

props.name: shimmer
props.comment: Shimmers the label — the "work is in flight" affordance. Implies busy.

props.name: intent
props.comment: Semantic color for system notes ("Rate limit reached").

components.name: clipboard-button
components.description: Copy-to-clipboard button

props.name: copiedText
props.comment: `wirekit::Copied`, the key `color-picker` uses too. A second catalog key for the same visible state would mean an application translating the kit has to find both, and the two components would answer the same event in two registers.

props.name: iconOnly
props.comment: Bare icon button — no border / bg / label, just the copy glyph (muted, pops green on copy). For compact action rows (a message's copy control). Requires an aria-label (there is no visible text to name it).

components.name: collapsible
components.description: Single disclosure — one trigger toggles one collapsible region (WAI-ARIA Disclosure)

props.name: trigger
props.comment: Trigger label (string). For rich trigger content, pass a named "trigger" slot instead — both surface as the $trigger variable, so the template renders either.

props.name: open
props.comment: Whether the region starts expanded. The default comes from the configuration, so an application whose boxes start open sets it once rather than at every call.

props.name: findable
props.comment: Closed content stays findable by the browser's find in page, which opens the disclosure a match lands in. Only where the engine supports it; switch it off for a spoiler.

components.name: countdown
components.description: Live countdown to an absolute deadline with overdue + urgent states (client-side, no polling)

props.name: until
props.comment: The ABSOLUTE target instant — a date object of any class, an ISO-8601 string, or a unix timestamp. Absolute, never a duration: a duration drifts the moment the tab sleeps or the page is cached; an absolute instant is recomputed from the real clock on every tick.

props.name: expiredText
props.comment: Text shown once the deadline has passed. Null → a translatable default.

props.name: warnThreshold
props.comment: Seconds-remaining threshold below which the countdown enters its "urgent" (warning-tinted) state. Null → no urgent state.

props.name: units
props.comment: Which units to show. 'auto' (default): the largest meaningful unit down to the smallest, dropping leading zero-units — years appear only once the remaining time actually reaches a year (no more "26831d"). Or an explicit ordered subset, e.g. "days hours minutes" or "years days": the largest listed unit carries all the overflow above it, the smallest truncates.

props.name: showSeconds
props.comment: Include seconds in 'auto' mode (ignored when `units` is an explicit list).

props.name: variant
props.comment: 'inline' (default): "73y 190d 12h 15m 09s". 'segments': each unit in its own boxed block with a label — the classic dashboard countdown look.

props.name: separators
props.comment: Locale-aware thousands separators on large unit values (like price). Turn off with :separators="false".

props.name: locale
props.comment: BCP-47 locale for the separators. Null → the app locale.

props.name: timezone
props.comment: The zone the deadline is written in for the reader, a name such as "Europe/Berlin": the deadline in the accessible name and the `datetime` of the time element. Null → the zone of the value given. The countdown itself counts to the same instant either way.

props.name: animate
props.comment: Change animation. For the segments variant, choose the style: true / "box"  → the whole box pulses (border + accent flash + scale pop) "text"        → only the changing number briefly flashes the accent color false / "none" → no motion The inline variant changes its value without motion.

props.name: pausable
props.comment: A way to stop the clock, for a countdown that stands beside other content and whose ticking the reader's task does not need, the end of a sale under a price (WCAG 2.2.2). `pausable` puts a button after the time that stops it and starts it again. `static` works the time out once, on the reader's clock as the page loads, and leaves it standing, for a page served from a cache that cannot work it out on the server. At the deadline either turns to its expired text, once, and fires its event.

props.name: as
props.comment: The element the countdown roots in. A `span` by default, because everything it renders inside is text-level, so a countdown can stand in a sentence: a `div` there would end the paragraph around it. `div` for a headless slot that holds block content.

components.name: data-list
components.description: Key-value data display list

components.name: empty-state
components.description: Placeholder for empty content areas

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1–6). Defaults to 3, an <h3>; set it to match the surrounding document outline so screen-reader heading navigation stays correct (e.g. level=2 directly under a page <h1>, or level=1 when the empty-state IS the page's main content).

props.name: variant
