props.comment: Container chrome: default (no border/bg) · outline (dashed border, reads as a placeholder drop-zone) · muted (filled muted surface).

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation. Null = no animation (default).

components.name: flag
components.description: Country or region flag, with a same-size placeholder for a code there is no artwork for

props.name: country
props.comment: A code the shipped artwork carries: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `de`, or one of its region and organization codes such as `eu` or `gb-sct`. Case does not matter.

props.name: src
props.comment: A URL to a flag of your own, for one the package does not carry. Wins over `country`.

props.name: shape
props.comment: `rect` shows the 4:3 artwork, `square` the 1:1 artwork, and `circle` crops the 1:1 artwork round. No artwork is stretched to a ratio it was not drawn for.

props.name: alt
props.comment: Empty by default, which makes the flag decorative: next to the country's name, a second announcement of the same name is noise. Give the flag a name when it stands alone.

components.name: image
components.description: Content image as a figure with alt text, lazy loading, CLS-safe ratio box, and optional caption

props.name: src
props.comment: Image URL. The component only renders — the developer supplies a ready URL (a signed / ACL-protected download URL works unchanged).

props.name: alt
props.comment: Accessible name. REQUIRED for a content image; pass an empty string ONLY for a purely decorative image (renders alt="" so screen readers skip it). The default is null rather than '' so the two cases can be told apart. With '' as the default, "the developer marked this decorative" and "the developer forgot" would produce identical markup — and the forgotten one is a content image that announces nothing, which no automated check can see either, because `alt=""` IS valid HTML and IS the correct answer for the other case.

props.name: caption
props.comment: Optional visible caption — renders a <figcaption> under the image.

props.name: altLang
props.comment: The language of `alt` and of `caption` where either differs from the page's, written on the and on the

props.name: ratio
props.comment: Optional intrinsic aspect-ratio ("16/9", "4/3", "1/1", or a number). Sizes the box BEFORE the image loads, so the layout never shifts (CLS-safe) even when the natural dimensions are unknown. Null → the image sizes itself.

props.name: fit
props.comment: object-fit for a ratio-boxed image: 'cover' (fill + crop) or 'contain' (letterbox, no crop). Ignored without a ratio.

props.name: rounded
props.comment: Corner rounding token: false (none) or true (--radius-wk-md).

props.name: loading
props.comment: Native lazy-loading. Eager only for above-the-fold hero images.

props.name: srcset
props.comment: Responsive sources and the width the image takes in the layout, written on the : srcset="a-800.jpg 800w, a-1600.jpg 1600w" with sizes="(min-width: 60rem) 50vw, 100vw".

props.name: width
props.comment: The image's intrinsic size in pixels, written on the . The browser reserves the box from their ratio before the file arrives, which is what keeps a layout without `ratio` from shifting.

props.name: fetchpriority
props.comment: Fetch priority for the image a page shows first: 'high', 'low' or 'auto'. Null leaves the choice to the browser.

props.name: sources
props.comment: Art direction: another file, often another crop, for a media condition. Each entry is an array with `srcset` and, as it needs them, `media`, `sizes`, `type` (`image/avif`) and the file's `width` and `height` in pixels. They render as `<source>` elements in a `<picture>` before the image, and the browser loads the first that matches, else `src`. With `width` and `height` on each, the box takes the ratio of the source the browser chose before the file arrives, so a portrait crop on a phone and a landscape one on a desk do not move the page as they load. `alt`, `loading` and `fetchpriority` stay on the image.

props.name: as
props.comment: The element the image roots in. A `figure` by default. `span` where the image stands in text-level content, such as inside a button, which takes no figure; the root then renders as a block, and a caption as a plain line under the image.

components.name: image-compare
components.description: Before/after image comparison slider

props.name: ratio
props.comment: Optional intrinsic aspect-ratio (e.g. "16/9", "4/3", "1/1"). The component has absolutely-positioned images, so it needs a sized box. Set `ratio` and the figure sizes ITSELF (height derived from width) — no hand-rolled `<div style="aspect-ratio: …">` wrapper needed. Leave it null to fill the height of whatever box the developer provides (the original contract).

props.name: name
props.comment: Form field name for the hidden input below. Declared as a prop rather than left to the attribute bag on purpose: the bag lands on the <figure>, where a `name` submits nothing, so a caller writing `name="reveal"` got a figure with a name attribute and a POST body without the field.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Locks the slider as `disabled` locks a native field: the handle and the track take no press and no key and leave the tab order, and the hidden input is not submitted. A disabled fieldset around the component locks it the same way.

components.name: image-hotspots
components.description: Image with markers that name what it shows, each a button that hands its target to the page, and a strip of the targets on the phone

props.name: src
props.comment: The image, its text alternative and its size in pixels, which reserves the box before the file arrives.

props.name: phoneSrc
props.comment: The file a phone shows, below 48rem: often another crop, with a size of its own. Each marker takes a position of its own on it, `phoneX` and `phoneY`.

props.name: fetchpriority
props.comment: `high` for an image at the top of the page, which the browser then fetches first.

props.name: markers
props.comment: The markers in the order Tab reaches them. Each one an array with `x` and `y`, the position of its center in percent of the image, and `label`, the name of its target, and as it needs them `phoneX`, `phoneY`, `target`, handed back in the event, `href` and `image` for its card.

props.name: icon
props.comment: The icon each marker shows.

props.name: label
props.comment: The name of the markers as a group, and of the strip of their targets on the phone.

props.name: strip
props.comment: The strip of targets under the image on the phone, each a link where it has an `href`.

components.name: image-gallery
components.description: Responsive image grid with an accessible, keyboard-navigable lightbox

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: The empty state. `empty` REPLACES the body rather than sitting beside it: the screen a new user sees FIRST is the one with no data, and a single muted sentence can only say that nothing is here — it cannot say what to do about it, which is the whole job of that screen. `emptyText` is the default, so a caller that does not care changes nothing. Same shape as data-table, which is where the reasoning was first written down.

props.name: images
props.comment: List of images: each an array with 'src' (required), 'alt' (required for a content image), and optional 'caption' and 'full'. A plain string is treated as a src with an empty alt (decorative) — pass the array form for real content. 'altLang' and 'captionLang' name the language of either text where it differs from the page's, in the grid and in the lightbox; a 'caption' may be an Htmlable. 'full' is the address the LIGHTBOX loads, and it defaults to 'src'. A grid tile is a few hundred pixels wide with ten of them on a page; the zoom view is the whole screen. Serving one address to both is the compromise an image ladder exists to end.

props.name: columns
props.comment: Responsive grid column spec, forwarded to the grid component (e.g. "2 md:3 lg:4"). Literal handling lives in grid — never interpolated here.

props.name: ratio
props.comment: Thumbnail aspect-ratio (CLS-safe). Null → images size themselves.

props.name: fit
props.comment: object-fit forwarded to each thumbnail. 'cover' (default) crops to a uniform grid — right for mixed-orientation photo sets. Use 'contain' when a single image must be shown whole (e.g. one portrait shot the crop would slice) — the thumbnail then letterboxes inside its ratio box instead.

props.name: lightbox
props.comment: Enable the click-to-zoom lightbox. When false the grid is static.

props.name: itemOverlay
props.comment: Per-item overlay render-callback: a closure `fn($item, $i)` that returns the markup to layer OVER thumbnail #$i (a badge, a report control, an "AI-generated" label). It renders as a sibling of the zoom trigger — not nested inside it — so the overlay wrapper is pointer-events-none and the thumbnail still opens the lightbox; interactive controls inside the overlay opt back in with `pointer-events-auto`. Return a view or HtmlString for HTML (a plain string is escaped). Null → no overlay. It covers the THUMBNAIL only; the zoom view takes `zoomOverlay` below.

props.name: zoomOverlay
props.comment: The zoom view's own overlay: the same `fn($item, $i)` shape as itemOverlay, laid over the image in the lightbox instead of over the thumbnail. A separate callback because the two surfaces differ (an overlay written for a square tile can sit wrong over a full-screen photo) and itemOverlay never reached the zoom view. A label that has to travel with the image, an "AI-generated" marking or a license note, goes to both. Ignored on a static grid, which has no zoom view. Null → no overlay.

props.name: zoomable
props.comment: Zoom inside the image the lightbox shows: buttons, the keys `+` `-` `0`, the wheel, a double click or a double tap, a pinch, and dragging the enlarged image. Handed to the lightbox with `maxZoom`, the largest scale as a multiple of the fitted size. Ignored on a static grid.

components.name: live-list
components.description: A list the server re-renders while it is read — keeps the reader's place when entries arrive above, and points to new entries out of sight

props.name: live
props.comment: This render answers a live event: keep the reader's place and report fresh rows out of sight.

components.name: product-card
components.description: Ecommerce product card — image, price with compare-at, rating, stock state, CTA

props.name: name
props.comment: What it is. Rendered as the heading and used as the image's fallback name.

props.name: href
props.comment: Where the product page is. The name becomes the link — see below for why the whole card is not one.

props.name: image
props.comment: Cover image URL.

props.name: imageAlt
props.comment: Accessible name for the image. Defaults to empty, NOT to the product name: the name is already right there in text, so repeating it makes a screen reader read the product twice. Pass it when the image shows something the name does not ("Blue, worn open over a white shirt").

props.name: price
props.comment: Price in the currency's major units, or minor units with :minor-units.

props.name: compareAt
props.comment: The price before the reduction. Renders struck through, and the saving is announced.

props.name: from
props.comment: The price is the lowest of several, the cheapest variant's: it reads "from €19.99".

props.name: unitPrice
props.comment: The unit price (Grundpreis) for goods sold by weight, volume, length or area, and the unit it refers to ("1 kg"), written beside the price as `price` writes it.

props.name: locale
props.comment: The locale every amount is written in, handed to each `price` with the currency. Unset, an amount follows the application's locale, as a `price` of its own would.

props.name: rating
props.comment: Average rating out of 5, and how many people gave it.

props.name: description
props.comment: Short line under the name.

props.name: availability
props.comment: 'in-stock' | 'low-stock' | 'out-of-stock'. Out of stock disables the CTA.

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 3 — a card in a grid of products — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

components.name: energy-label
components.description: EU energy label arrow beside a price — the class in its color, the scale, links to the label and the product information sheet

props.name: efficiency
props.comment: The product's energy efficiency class as its label shows it: `A` to `G`, or a class of an older scale such as `A+++`.

props.name: scale
props.comment: The scale of the label, best class first: `A-G` for the labels in force since 2021, or an older seven-class scale, `A+++-D`, `A++-E` or `A+-F`.

props.name: href
props.comment: The address of the label itself, an image or a PDF. The arrow links to it, which is how the labeling acts let a shop show the label behind the arrow: on a click, a hover or a tap.

props.name: sheet
props.comment: The address of the product information sheet, the product's page in the EU product database for instance. Linked beside the arrow under the name the acts prescribe.

props.name: size
props.comment: The size of the price beside it, as on `price`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`. The class on the arrow stands in that size.

props.name: direction
props.comment: `right` points the arrow right with the range on its left; `left` mirrors it.

props.name: newTab
props.comment: Opens the label and the sheet in another tab, for a page that must not be left.

components.name: tire-label
components.description: EU tire label arrows beside a price — fuel efficiency, wet grip and noise classes with their ranges, links to the label and the product information sheet

props.name: fuel
props.comment: The fuel efficiency class on the tire's label, `A` to `E`.

props.name: wetGrip
props.comment: The wet grip class on the tire's label, `A` to `E`.

props.name: noise
props.comment: The external rolling noise class on the tire's label, `A` to `C`.

props.name: noiseDb
props.comment: The external rolling noise in decibels, shown after the loudspeaker.

props.name: href
props.comment: The address of the label itself, an image or a PDF. Each arrow links to it, which is how a shop shows the label behind the arrows: on a click, a hover or a tap.

props.name: sheet
props.comment: The address of the product information sheet, the tire's page in the EU product database for instance. Linked beside the arrows under the name the regulation prescribes.

props.name: size
props.comment: The size of the price beside it, as on `price`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`. The classes on the arrows stand in that size.

props.name: newTab
props.comment: Opens the label and the sheet in another tab, for a page that must not be left.

components.name: review
components.description: One customer review as an article — stars, title, author, date, a verified-purchase badge and the shop's reply

props.name: rating
props.comment: The review's score, as `rating` shows one.

props.name: max
props.comment: The top of the scale, as on `rating`.

props.name: title
props.comment: The title, the review's heading.

props.name: author
props.comment: The reviewer's display name.

props.name: date
props.comment: When it was written: a date, a string Carbon reads, or a Unix timestamp.

props.name: verified
props.comment: A purchase the shop has verified: a badge says so in words.

props.name: level
props.comment: The heading level of the title, the one the page's outline needs.

props.name: replyAuthor
props.comment: Who replied for the shop, and when. The reply itself is the `reply` slot.

props.name: timezone
props.comment: The zone the dates are written in. Null keeps each date's own.

components.name: review-summary
components.description: Reviews at a glance — the average as stars, the count, and the distribution of stars, each row a filter link

props.name: average
props.comment: The mean score, as `rating` shows one. Null while there are no reviews.

props.name: count
props.comment: The number of reviews. Null takes the sum of the distribution. It may be larger, when reviews without stars are counted.

props.name: distribution
props.comment: Stars => number of reviews, `[5 => 82, 4 => 30, 3 => 9, 2 => 4, 1 => 3]`. A step that is missing counts 0.

props.name: max
props.comment: The top of the scale, as on `rating`.

props.name: filters
props.comment: Stars => the address that lists the reviews with that many stars. A row with one is a link.

props.name: current
props.comment: The stars the list is filtered by, marked on its row.

components.name: swatch
components.description: A color or pattern value with its name, as a circle or a square

props.name: color
props.comment: The value's color: a hex color, rgb(), hsl() or oklch(). It is written into the swatch's style, so any other value is rejected and the swatch draws no fill.

props.name: image
props.comment: A picture of the value, such as a fabric or a wood grain, that fills the swatch. Given with a `color`, the color lies behind it: it shows through the picture's transparent parts, while the picture loads and where it does not load. An address with a scheme other than http or https draws nothing.

props.name: label
props.comment: The value's name. It names the swatch for assistive technology, or stands beside it as text with `showLabel`, and a pill draws it as its text. Without a name the swatch is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: showLabel
props.comment: Show the name as text beside the swatch. A pill shows it inside already.

props.name: unavailable
props.comment: A line across the swatch, or through a pill's text, and "unavailable" read with its name.

props.name: size
props.comment: `sm` (24px), `md` (32px) or `lg` (40px), the height of a pill.

props.name: shape
props.comment: `circle`, `square`, or `pill`, which draws the name as text, for a value a name says best, such as a size. A color or a picture given with a pill is a dot before the name.

components.name: page-progress
components.description: Page-edge bar reporting the request the reader is waiting on (navigation + Livewire round trips)

props.name: intent
props.comment: primary | neutral | success | warning | danger | info | auto

props.name: showAfter
props.comment: Milliseconds of waiting before the bar appears at all. Most requests finish inside this window and show nothing, which is the point: a bar that blinks on every click is noise, and noise is what stops the reader noticing the one request that really is slow.

props.name: ceiling
props.comment: The percentage the easing approaches while it waits. It is a ceiling rather than a destination — a round trip has no percentage, and 100 has to keep meaning "finished" instead of "the animation ran out".

components.name: progress
components.description: Progress bar with optional value display

props.name: value
props.comment: numeric value (0..max). null = indeterminate

props.name: max
props.comment: max value the bar represents

props.name: label
props.comment: visible label rendered above the bar

props.name: showValue
props.comment: show "42 / 100" next to label

props.name: variant
props.comment: back-compat alias of `intent`

props.name: intent

components.name: reading-shell
components.description: Composition wrapper with toggles + density preset

props.name: progress
props.comment: Toggles default to null so the density preset's per-primitive default wins. An explicit bool (`:spine="false"`) overrides the density's baseline. Net effect for the developer: `density="minimal"` actually hides things; passing the toggle explicitly always wins.

props.name: boundary
props.comment: `boundary` — pass-through to the composed primitives (reading-progress, reading-spine, reading-bookmark). Default `null` keeps the viewport- pinned behavior. Set to `'container'` to scope every composed primitive to the shell's nearest positioned ancestor — required when embedding the entire reading surface inside a modal body, sidebar pane, preview iframe, or Livewire panel.

props.name: layout
props.comment: `layout` — the spine's. `ticks` pins it to the page's edge; `rail` makes it an outline in a column beside the slot, which the shell builds (see below).

components.name: reading-spine
components.description: Sidebar mini-TOC tracking scroll, expanding on hover/focus

props.name: exclude
props.comment: A selector for subtrees whose headings are NOT this page's structure, such as live component demos, whose accordion panel titles or carousel product names would otherwise become entries. `target` cannot help there, because the demos sit INSIDE the article that holds the real sections. Unset (the default), every heading in `target` is an entry.

props.name: edgeOffset
props.comment: How far in from the edge `position` chose. `position` picks WHICH edge; this picks the distance, and `0` is expressible: a spine flush against the window. An unlayered stylesheet override would reach every spine in the app rather than the one call that wants it, and it wins only because Tailwind v4 emits its utilities into a layer. Null keeps 1rem.

props.name: offset
props.comment: NOT the distance from the edge — that is `edgeOffset` above. This is the scroll/observer offset the plugin measures a section's arrival against.

props.name: boundary
props.comment: `boundary` — null (default) = viewport-pinned via Tailwind `fixed`. `'container'` = scoped to the nearest positioned ancestor via Tailwind `absolute`. Use `'container'` when embedding the spine inside a contained reading surface (a modal body, a sidebar pane, a docs preview frame) so it doesn't escape to the outer viewport.

props.name: layout
props.comment: `ticks` (the default) is the classic spine: pinned to an edge of the window or a container, a column of ticks that expands on hover. `rail` is an outline in the page's own flow, for a grid column beside the article: every entry stays visible on a line that bends with the indent, and a band on that line slides to the current section. The rail places itself where the page puts it, so `expand`, `boundary`, `position` and `edge-offset` do nothing there.

components.name: reading-toc
components.description: Horizontal sticky-strip TOC for marketing landing pages

props.name: flush
props.comment: `flush` — when true, the strip runs viewport-edge-to-viewport-edge: zero horizontal padding on the nav AND the inner list AND the first / last link. The strip's chrome (background + bottom border) and the visible "Features" / "Pricing" / "…" text both run flush to the viewport boundary. Use when the TOC sits below an edge-to-edge marketing-page chrome (brand-bar with no `padding="lg"` setting, or sandwiched between a hero and the article body). The hover-state background keeps its internal padding on the opposite edge so the rounded background still has breathing room around the rendered text. Default `false` pads every link symmetrically.

components.name: reorder
components.description: Drag handle and move-up / move-down arrows for one row of a list Livewire sorts, so a keyboard and a screen reader can reorder it too

props.name: item
props.comment: The row's key: the value its row carries in `wire:sort:item`.

props.name: position
props.comment: Where the row stands, counted from 0, and how many rows there are. The first row cannot move up and the last cannot move down, so those arrows are disabled. Without `count` the down arrow is never disabled, because nothing here knows which row is last.

props.name: action
props.comment: The Livewire method the list's `wire:sort` names. The arrows call it with the two arguments a drop passes, the row's key and its new position, so one method serves the pointer and the keyboard.

props.name: label
props.comment: What the row is, for the arrows' names: "Move Photo 3 up". Without it they are "Move up" and "Move down", which is enough where the row itself says what it is.

props.name: arrowSurface
props.comment: The arrows' button surface and size, handed to both. An application whose icon buttons use another surface sets it here: a class on this element does not reach the buttons inside it.

components.name: replay-button
components.description: Re-mount the closest [data-replay-target] ancestor — companion to the `data-replayable` animation contract

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible label for the button. Default is the well-known "Replay" verb so screen readers announce a clear affordance.

props.name: target
props.comment: Optional explicit data-replay-target selector when the closest ancestor isn't the right re-mount root. Pass a CSS selector and the click handler walks up via $el.closest(selector) instead.

components.name: scroll-area
components.description: Scrollable content area with styled scrollbar

props.name: orientation
props.comment: vertical | horizontal | both

props.name: fade
props.comment: Edge fade: false (none) | 'both' | 'start' | 'end' | 'auto'. Masks the overflow edge(s) along the scroll axis so the content itself dissolves into the background — a background-agnostic "there's more to scroll" hint (mask-image, not a colored overlay). Removed on :focus-within so a keyboard-focused child near an edge is never clipped by the mask. The named edges are pure CSS and unconditional, which is also their limit: they fade an edge the content does not continue past — at the very top, at the very bottom, and on an area whose content fits and cannot scroll at all. 'auto' opts into an Alpine plugin that measures instead and fades only where there really is more. Without JavaScript it renders no mask, which is the right way round: a missing hint beats dissolved text.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the scroll region, and the switch that makes it a LANDMARK. `role="region"` plus a name is a landmark, so a built-in name would make ten scroll areas on one page ten rotor entries all called "Scrollable content" — axe reports it as `landmark-unique`, and the name meant to tell them apart would make them identical. Without a name the element keeps `tabindex="0"` and no role: still keyboard-reachable (WCAG 2.1.1), just deliberately not a destination. Name it after the CONTENT ("Release notes"), never after the mechanism.

components.name: segmented-control
components.description: Segmented toggle control

props.name: error
props.comment: `error` is declared like `label`: undeclared, `:error` on this control would land in the attribute bag and render as a stray HTML attribute — a validation message the developer wrote, silently not shown, on a control that is part of forms.

props.name: announceError
props.comment: A11y: render the error message in a polite live region by default so a server-side validation error that appears after submit (when focus is elsewhere) is announced. Mirrors the input component. Set false to opt out — an app that runs its OWN error summary would otherwise double-announce here.

props.name: help
props.comment: Explained in a tooltip from a question mark beside the label, and read as the field's description (partials/field-help).

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: Livewire method to call optimistically. The segment moves immediately and is put back if the call fails. Absent -> the component renders without an optimistic layer. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

props.name: disabled
props.comment: Disable the whole control: aria-disabled on the radiogroup + each segment, the buttons become non-interactive, and the group dims via --opacity-wk-disabled.

props.name: label

components.name: shimmer
components.description: Animated text-glyph shimmer for live/streaming status (background-clip:text, Livewire :active-bindable)

props.name: active
props.comment: Whether the shimmer sweep animates across the text glyphs. Bind it to a Livewire property — :active="$isStreaming" — to run the effect ONLY while streaming / loading and settle to plain text when done. This is the Livewire-native differentiator: the React-only equivalents toggle the effect by conditionally rendering the class; here the server drives it.

props.name: as
props.comment: The wrapper tag. Defaults to an inline <span> so a shimmer drops into a sentence ("Generating response…"); use as="div"/"p" for block text.

props.name: duration
props.comment: Animation duration — any CSS <time>. Overrides the --shimmer-wk-duration token for THIS instance only (slower = calmer, faster = more urgent).

components.name: chart-mixed

props.name: valueGrouping

props.name: tooltipExtras

components.name: stat

props.name: trend
props.comment: 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral' | null

props.name: animate
props.comment: Opt-in counter animation. When true, the value text is wrapped in an Alpine x-data="wirekitStatAnimate" handler that animates 0 → value over 1.2s once the stat scrolls into view. Respects prefers-reduced-motion (snaps to value, no animation).

props.name: descriptionDeferred
props.comment: Description animation Option A — defer fade-in. When true AND animate=true, the description span is hidden via x-show while the counter runs (~1.2s) and fades in once the animation settles. Mutually exclusive with descriptionAnimate.

props.name: descriptionAnimate
props.comment: Description animation Option C — synchronous color count-up. When true AND animate=true, the description text color interpolates from --color-wk-text-muted → --color-wk-text on the same 1.2s timeline as the value. Mutually exclusive with descriptionDeferred.

props.name: animateIn
props.comment: Optional reveal animation when stat scrolls into view (separate from the value count-up `animate` prop). Null = no reveal (default).

props.name: intent
props.comment: KPI-tile chrome: when set, the stat gains an intent-colored 4-sided border + a faint intent-tinted body — the pattern dashboard blueprints hand-rolled per tile. null = the existing plain card surface, unchanged. primary | success | warning | danger | info | neutral.

props.name: href

props.name: pressed
props.comment: The tile as a toggle, a figure above a list that sets the filter it counts: true or false renders a `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed`, and a pressed tile draws the frame of a selection in place of the neutral border. A caller's `wire:click`, `wire:key` and `data-*` land on the button, and its name is what it shows, as a linked tile's is. Null keeps the tile as it is.

props.name: fit
props.comment: Shrinks the value from `value` down to a floor so it fits its line: true for the `--text-wk-fit-floor` token, a length such as `1rem` for a floor of its own, null or false for none. A value written in the slot keeps its size.

components.name: stats

props.name: intent
props.comment: Color role. Same vocabulary as badge / button, so a call site that knows one knows this.

components.name: status-dot
components.description: Status dot that sits in the line beside a value, named for a screen reader and explained in a tooltip

props.name: intent
props.comment: The state the dot stands for, in the intents a badge takes.

props.name: label
props.comment: What the dot means, in words: its accessible name, and the text of its tooltip. Without a label the dot is decorative and hidden from assistive technology, so the meaning has to be said somewhere else on the page.

props.name: tooltip
props.comment: Show the label in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus. Only a labeled dot has one.

props.name: placement
props.comment: Where the tooltip opens. Above by default: beside a number in a cell aligned to the end, a panel opening to the side lands on the number it explains.

props.name: focusable
props.comment: Whether the dot takes a tab stop of its own, so a keyboard reaches its tooltip. Set false inside a link or a button: the control is the tab stop there, and the dot's name is part of the control's name.

props.name: size
props.comment: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 10px.

components.name: status-matrix
components.description: 2D grid of typed status cells (tristate / toggle / status / heat) with sticky headers

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: The empty state. `empty` REPLACES the body rather than sitting beside it: the screen a new user sees FIRST is the one with no data, and a single muted sentence can only say that nothing is here — it cannot say what to do about it, which is the whole job of that screen. `emptyText` is the default, so a caller that does not care changes nothing. Same shape as data-table, which is where the reasoning was first written down.

props.name: rows
props.comment: [{key,label}] — the matrix rows (left axis)

props.name: columns
props.comment: [{key,label}] — the matrix columns (top axis)

props.name: cells
props.comment: value map: ["rowKey:colKey" => value] OR [rowKey => [colKey => value]]

props.name: cellType
props.comment: tristate | toggle | status | heat

props.name: editable
props.comment: tristate / toggle become interactive

props.name: cornerLabel
props.comment: top-left header cell label (the row-axis name)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.comment: Accessible name for the grid, and the switch that makes the scroll wrapper a LANDMARK. Two elements read this prop, and they treat it differently on purpose. The inner `<table>` is ALWAYS named — a table with no accessible name is a worse outcome than a duplicated region, so the fallback below survives for it. The outer scroll wrapper only becomes `role="region"` when the CALLER named it: unnamed, three matrices on one page were three rotor entries called "Status matrix" (axe: `landmark-unique`).

props.name: name
props.comment: hidden-input name for form submission (editable)

props.name: heatFrom
props.comment: low end (cold)

props.name: heatTo
props.comment: high end (hot)

props.name: heatMin

props.name: heatMax
props.comment: heat scale upper bound

props.name: heatUnit
props.comment: suffix on heat value labels (e.g. '%')

props.comment: render the cell-type legend

components.name: status-tiles
components.description: N entities as colored status tiles, one glance — a fleet light with optional legend and colorblind-safe status icons

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: The empty state. `empty` REPLACES the body rather than sitting beside it: the screen a new user sees FIRST is the one with no data, and a single muted sentence can only say that nothing is here — it cannot say what to do about it, which is the whole job of that screen. `emptyText` is the default, so a caller that does not care changes nothing. Same shape as data-table.

props.name: items
props.comment: The fleet: a list of entities to render as status tiles. Each entry: ['key' => 'app-1', 'label' => __('wirekit::shop.example'), 'intent' => 'danger', 'href' => '…', 'meta' => '2 issues'] intent ∈ success | warning | danger | info | neutral (anything else → neutral). 'href' makes the tile a keyboard-operable link; 'meta' is an optional caption.

props.name: legend
props.comment: Show a count-per-intent legend above the grid (only intents present are listed).

props.name: columns
props.comment: Responsive grid column spec, forwarded verbatim to the grid component (never interpolated here — the literal-class safelist lives in grid).

props.name: showStatus
props.comment: Promote the status word from the screen-reader-only span into a visible, intent-tinted caption on every tile. Off by default: the word is then for screen readers only.

props.name: wrapMeta
props.comment: Let the caption wrap instead of clamping it to one line. Off by default, and that default is load-bearing rather than caution: a wrapping caption grows the whole grid row, so flipping it for everyone would move every dashboard that uses this. On for the case the clamp destroys — when the caption IS the message ("Used disk space: 87% on /var") rather than a two-word count.

components.name: stream
components.description: Streaming text output (SSE) with correct live-region a11y, reduced-motion buffering, and defined abort / error states

props.name: url
props.comment: The Server-Sent Events endpoint to stream from. Null → the component stays idle (seed it with `initial-text` and drive it from your own controls).

props.name: eventName
props.comment: SSE event name to listen for, and the payload that ends the stream.

props.name: announce
props.comment: How the result is announced to assistive tech once the stream settles: 'result' (default) — announce the final text once. 'status'           — announce only "Response ready". 'none'             — announce nothing, and render NO live region. 'none' exists for one situation and is wrong everywhere else: an application that already has its own status region for this response. Two regions announcing the same completion is not twice the accessibility — a screen-reader user hears it twice and cannot tell which one is the real one. Pair it with the `output` slot, which replaces the visible block for the same reason. If you use it and do NOT announce completion yourself, the response finishes silently for anyone not watching the screen. That is the trade, stated rather than buried: this prop hands the announcement contract to the caller, it does not delete it.

props.name: autoStart
props.comment: Open the stream on init. Set false to start it from your own control.

props.name: initialText
props.comment: Seed text — resume a completed response (SSR) or show a static example.

props.name: source
props.comment: Where the tokens come from: 'sse' (default) — the browser's EventSource. GET-only and body-less. 'fetch'         — POST (or any method) and read the response body. The shape LLM APIs use, because the request IS the payload: prompt, options and model belong in a body, not a URL. 'manual'        — no transport at all. Feed the component yourself with push()/finish()/fail() or the wirekit-stream-* events, e.g. from Laravel's own Reverb/Echo WebSocket stack.

props.name: method
props.comment: fetch mode only — request shape.

props.name: name
props.comment: Names this stream so the wirekit-stream-* events can address one of several on the same page (a pane per voice).

props.name: simulate
props.comment: Simulate mode: stream THIS text token-by-token from a local timer, with no SSE endpoint. Drives a live-looking demo (and a typewriter effect), and opts the component into the docs "↻ Replay" affordance so a reader can re-watch it.

props.name: simulateSpeed
props.comment: Milliseconds per token in simulate mode (default 55).

props.name: startMessage
props.comment: What the screen reader is told at each turn of the state machine. Each defaults to the shipped catalog, so an application that publishes the lang files gets its own language with no prop at all — these exist for the copy that differs per surface ("Translating…" rather than "Generating response…"). The failure ones were unreachable: the announcement and all five reasons were literals in the JavaScript, so every failure spoke English no matter what language the rest of the interface was in — in the one moment the reader most needs to understand what happened.

components.name: strength-meter
components.description: Strength meter — bars for how hard a value is to guess, with the step named and spoken; the display password-input uses

props.name: value
props.comment: The lit steps, from 0 (nothing to judge yet) to `max`. Whole steps: a fraction rounds.

props.name: max
props.comment: How many bars, and so how many steps.

props.name: label
props.comment: The meter's accessible name, and the subject of what it says when the step changes: "Code strength: Strong". A step's word alone would not say what it judges.

props.name: levels
props.comment: What each step is called, weakest first, one per bar. Four bars default to Weak, Fair, Good and Strong; any other count defaults to "2 of 5".

props.name: showLevel
props.comment: Show the current step's word beside the bars as well.

props.name: announce
props.comment: Speak a changed step through a polite status region. Off where the page already says it.

components.name: swap
components.description: Two-state icon primitive — fade (crossfade), rotate or flip between two children

props.name: expression
props.comment: An Alpine expression naming the state, e.g. expression="isDark". Use this whenever the swap has to react to something on the client — which is nearly always, since a swap that cannot change is just an icon. It exists because `active` alone CANNOT work here: `active` is resolved in PHP at render time, so the swap would be frozen at whatever the server thought and never move again.

props.name: active
props.comment: Static state, for a swap the server already knows the answer to and that never changes on the client.

props.name: effect
props.comment: How the two states trade places. 'fade'   — crossfade (the quiet default) 'rotate' — half a turn, for a sun/moon or a chevron 'flip'   — a card flip

components.name: table
components.description: Data table with sorting and styling options

props.name: fit
props.comment: As wide as its columns, at most as wide as the space, and beyond that as without it. A responsive table measures its columns against a container, and a container takes no width from what it holds, so a wrapper that sizes itself by its content (`w-fit`, `inline-block`) leaves the table no width at all. This is the way to the same layout from inside.

props.name: stickyHeaderMax
props.comment: How tall the scroll-confined body may get before it scrolls. `stickyHeader` needs a bounded height to mean anything at all — the wrapper already carries `overflow-x: auto`, which makes it a scroll container on BOTH axes, so a `sticky` heading measures itself against a box that never scrolls vertically and therefore never sticks. The height is the CONDITION, not the decoration. The default is `24rem`. A viewport-relative value like `70vh` is what a table of unknown length wants, because the limit then follows the screen and simply never applies to the short case. Any CSS length, taken exactly as written. The value reaches the element as an inline max-height rather than as a utility class, so it is not confined to the lengths a build has already seen — `calc(100vh - 4rem)` arrives with its spaces intact. A length the browser cannot parse is dropped like any other bad declaration, so an unusable value leaves no max-height rather than a wrong one. The reasoning is with the code below.

props.name: stickyColumn
props.comment: freeze the FIRST column while the rest scroll horizontally

props.name: stickyColumnBelow
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl — freeze it only below that breakpoint

props.name: stackBelow
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl — below that breakpoint every body row stands as a card and every cell as a line that names its column, so a wide table does not scroll sideways on a phone.

props.name: stackBelowContainer
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl | 3xl | 4xl | 5xl — the same, below a width of the TABLE rather than of the window, on the container scale of a column's `hideBelowContainer`: beside a sidebar or in one column of a page the window is the wrong thing to measure. A responsive table only, since its frame is what is measured.

props.name: alpineSort
props.comment: enable client-side Alpine sorting (no Livewire needed)

props.name: tableLabel
props.comment: Accessible name for the responsive scroll wrapper, and the switch that makes it a LANDMARK. The wrapper is keyboard-reachable either way (WCAG 2.1.1 — `tabindex="0"` is unconditional); the role only joins it once there is a name worth navigating to. A fallback such as "Scrollable table" would make every table on a page answer to the same rotor entry — axe reports that as `landmark-unique`. Name it after the DATA ("Customer list"), never after the widget.

props.name: variant
props.comment: `flush` drops the fill and keeps everything else — the divider, the sticky rules, the spacing. The fill was painted unconditionally, so a table head that needed no background could only be reached by overriding the whole class string, which also discards the sticky behavior and the border a reader relies on. One opinion about one property should not cost the rest of the component.

props.name: item
props.comment: The row's key: the value its row carries in `wire:sort:item`.

props.name: position
props.comment: Where the row stands, counted from 0, and how many rows there are. The first row cannot move up and the last cannot move down, so those arrows are disabled. Without `count` the down arrow is never disabled, because nothing here knows which row is last.

props.name: action
props.comment: The Livewire method the table body's `wire:sort` names. The arrows call it with the two arguments a drop passes, the row's key and its new position, so one method serves the pointer and the keyboard.

props.name: label
props.comment: What the row is, for the arrows' names: "Move Photo 3 up". Without it they are "Move up" and "Move down", which is enough where the row's own cells say what it is.

props.name: arrowSurface
props.comment: The arrows' button surface and size, handed to both. An application whose icon buttons use another surface sets it here: a class on the cell does not reach the buttons inside it.

props.name: detailsBelowContainer
props.comment:
* A SECOND row under this one, carrying what `hide-below[-container]` took off the
     * remaining columns.
     *
     * It is a slot on this component rather than a sibling `table.details`. A sibling
     * component reads better at the call site and cannot work: Tailwind's `divide-y` compiles
     * to `:where(.divide-y > :not(:last-child))` with `border-bottom-width`, so the line
     * between a record and its details belongs to the record row, and a sibling cannot reach
     * backwards to switch it off -- CSS has no previous-sibling combinator. One component
     * emitting both rows owns the border, the `:last-child` arithmetic and the stripe.

props.name: for
props.comment: The id of the table whose rows the field shortens: the `id` on the table component, which lands on its `<table>`. The id of an element around the table works as well.

props.name: label
props.comment: The field's name for a screen reader, and its placeholder unless `placeholder` names another.

props.name: emptyText
props.comment: What the field says beside itself, and announces, when no row matches the query.

props.name: belowContainer
props.comment: The table width below which the column this stands in for gives way: the same value as that column's `hideBelowContainer`. sm … 5xl.

props.name: from
props.comment: The window width from which it does, the same value as the column's `hideBelowContainerFrom`: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl.

props.name: below
props.comment: For a column that gives way to the window instead, the same value as its `hideBelow`: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl.

props.name: align
props.comment: left | center | right

props.name: hideBelow
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl — the same value as the column's header

props.name: hideBelowContainer
props.comment: Hide the column below a width of the TABLE, not of the window. `hideBelow` asks the viewport, and beside a sidebar that is the wrong question: in an app shell the table can have less room at a 1024px viewport than at 768px, because the sidebar steps beside the content at `lg`, so a column that appears at `md` appears exactly where the table has least room. The scale is the container scale and it is not the viewport one. Tailwind's container sizes are their own ladder: `3xl` here is 48rem of TABLE width, where `hide-below="md"` is 48rem of WINDOW. Same numbers, different subject — so the two props are deliberately not interchangeable and a call site should pick one. The container is NAMED (`@container/wk-table` on the table's frame) rather than anonymous: an unnamed container would also become the measuring context for every `@`-variant a caller nests inside the table, and silently retarget it.

props.name: hideBelowContainerFrom
props.comment: The window width from which `hideBelowContainer` applies: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl. Below it the column keeps its place, and the table scrolls in its own frame. A list that may scroll on a phone but not on a desk takes `hide-below-container="5xl"` with this at `xl`: the column gives way only in a window of 80rem and up. `table.stand-in` shows what stands in for it, there.

props.name: label
props.comment: The name of the cell's column where the table stacks its rows (`stack-below` on the table). Unset, the header above the column names it.

props.name: actions
props.comment: Stacked, the cell that holds the row's actions stands as the card's footer, without a name. Unset, that is a cell aligned to the end that carries no label of its own. `false` keeps a value aligned to the end, a column of figures, as a line named by its column, and `true` makes any cell the footer.

props.name: sortDirection
props.comment: null | 'asc' | 'desc' — current sort state (Livewire mode)

props.name: column
props.comment: column identifier for Alpine sort mode (pairs with table alpine-sort)

props.name: sortAction
props.comment: Livewire-sort mode only: the wire:click method call for a keyboard-operable sort button, e.g. "sortBy('name')". When set, the header label + indicator are wrapped in a <button wire:click> so the sort is reachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1) — the plain <th> click on a cursor-pointer cell is mouse-only. Null keeps a static <span> (the developer supplies their own control via $attributes). Ignored in Alpine-sort mode (the `column` prop already renders its own button model).

props.name: align
props.comment: left | center | right

props.name: headerScope
props.comment: HTML <th scope> attribute — 'col' (default) for a column header, 'row' for a per-row header cell (WCAG 1.3.1: a row-header cell identifies its data row). Distinct from the `scope` prop above, which is WireKit's token-scope override — overloading that would break scoped theming for the 200+ components that share it.

props.name: hideBelow
props.comment: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl — hide this column below that breakpoint; its cells take the same value.

props.name: hideBelowContainer
props.comment: Hide the column below a width of the TABLE, not of the window. `hideBelow` asks the viewport, and beside a sidebar that is the wrong question: in an app shell the table can have less room at a 1024px viewport than at 768px, because the sidebar steps beside the content at `lg`, so a column that appears at `md` appears exactly where the table has least room. The scale is the container scale and it is not the viewport one. Tailwind's container sizes are their own ladder: `3xl` here is 48rem of TABLE width, where `hide-below="md"` is 48rem of WINDOW. Same numbers, different subject — so the two props are deliberately not interchangeable and a call site should pick one. The container is NAMED (`@container/wk-table` on the table's frame) rather than anonymous: an unnamed container would also become the measuring context for every `@`-variant a caller nests inside the table, and silently retarget it.

props.name: hideBelowContainerFrom
props.comment: The window width from which `hideBelowContainer` applies: sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl. Below it the column keeps its place, and the table scrolls in its own frame. A list that may scroll on a phone but not on a desk takes `hide-below-container="5xl"` with this at `xl`: the column gives way only in a window of 80rem and up. `table.stand-in` shows what stands in for it, there.

props.name: wrap
props.comment: Let a long header break instead of holding its column as wide as the longest word. A column header is `whitespace-nowrap` by default, and that is right for the usual one-word head. It is wrong for a column whose NAME is long and whose CONTENT is not: a permissions table with heads like "Nutzungsbedingungen" over icons that need 16px holds each column at the width of its word, and the table runs past its frame rather than the heads taking two lines. `wrap` breaks ANYWHERE, which is what a long compound over a narrow icon column needs. `wrap="words"` breaks only between words and evens the lines up: over a column of numbers there is nothing to hold the column wider than a digit, and a head that may break anywhere fell to that width ("Line / s", "to 2 / %"). Between words, the longest word is the floor.

props.name: sideways
props.comment: Turn the label on its side, reading from bottom to top on one line. For a column whose NAME is long and whose values are a mark or a glyph, next to a column that takes the rest of the width, such as a user list with one column per legal text. `wrap` cannot help there, since the wide column claims everything the heads give up and they fall to one letter per line. A turned head is as wide as one line of text in any language, and the row grows instead. Every head in that row then stands on the row's floor (the stylesheet does that, from the row), and a sort indicator stays upright under the label. A turned head is one line, so it outranks `wrap`.

props.name: variant
props.comment: header | cell

props.name: help
props.comment: The help of a column: the question mark a `label` shows beside a field, beside the head, with this text in its tooltip. It stands beside a sort button and never inside it, so its click opens the help without sorting, and the button's name stays the head.

props.name: helpId
props.comment: The id of a hidden copy of `help`, which a field in each row of the column lists in its `aria-describedby`. Without it the help is the tooltip alone.

components.name: ticker
components.description: Compact label + value + delta widget for dashboards

props.name: trendLabel
props.comment: Names the sparkline in the default slot. Opt-in, and null by default: a graphic that already carries its own name must not be given a second, worse one — see the block that renders the slot.

components.name: testimonial
components.description: Cited customer quote — figure/blockquote semantics, author, role, logo, optional rating

props.name: author
props.comment: Who said it. An unattributed testimonial is just marketing copy in quotation marks, so this carries the whole credibility of the block.

props.name: role
props.comment: Their role / company ("CTO, Acme").

props.name: avatar
props.comment: Avatar image for the author. Without one, the author's initials are derived and rendered instead — never an empty gray circle.

props.name: initials
props.comment: Override the derived initials (non-Latin names, mononyms, brand accounts).

props.name: logo
props.comment: Company logo shown beside the attribution.

props.name: logoAlt
props.comment: Accessible name for the logo. Leave null when the author is already named in text (the logo is then decoration and stays silent); pass it when the logo is the ONLY attribution.

props.name: logoAspect
props.comment: Intrinsic aspect ratio of `$logo`, as `'width/height'` — e.g. `'3/1'`. Same reasoning as brand's `logoAspect`: the mark is `w-auto` at the `xs` height, so the height is fixed and the width comes from the image. Until its bytes arrive there is nothing to derive that width from, and the attribution row re-flows when they land. The min-width floor below keeps the worst case at a square rather than at nothing.

props.name: rating
props.comment: Optional star rating (0..5). Always read-only — a testimonial is a record, not an input.

components.name: testimonial-grid
components.description: Responsive grid of testimonials, exposed as a labeled list

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the set of quotes.

components.name: theme-controller
components.description: Drop-in dark-mode control — button, switch, menu or system/light/dark select

props.name: variant
props.comment: How the control looks. 'button' — an icon button that flips light/dark (the compact default) 'switch' — a labeled switch, for a settings row 'select' — System / Light / Dark in a native control 'menu'   — a trigger naming the mode that is on, with a menu of all three `select` and `menu` are the three-valued shapes: only they can say "system". A two-state control cannot, and that is not a gap to fill — it has to freeze the reader onto an explicit choice the moment they touch it, and then their machine going dark at sunset leaves this page behind.

props.name: size
props.comment: Button-variant chrome (ignored by switch/select/menu). size:    'sm' (32px) | 'md' (36px, default) — 36px is the button scale's `md-compact`, not its 40px `md` surface: 'filled' (bordered, elevated — the default) | 'ghost' (borderless, transparent, muted) so the toggle sits flush next to surface="ghost" size="sm" buttons in a top bar.

props.name: touchFloor
props.comment: On a touch screen, stand at the touch target's size, a 44px square, rather than at the drawn size with a hit area around it: for a toggle in a row of labeled buttons, which stand at 44px there, as `touch-floor` does on a button. The menu variant hands it to its trigger.

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name. The control has no visible text in the button variant, so without this it announces as "button" and nothing else.

props.name: hideLabel
props.comment: Render the switch/select label sr-only (kept as the control's accessible name) — for a header or toolbar where the surrounding chrome already says what the control is. The <label> WRAPS the control here, so the name is associated with the element rather than with the visible text and survives being taken off the screen. No-op on the button variant, which has no visible text at all. Mirrors input / select / textarea / combobox / checkbox `hideLabel`. On `menu` it hides something else, and the difference is worth knowing: there is no <label> and no `label` prop in play at all. What it takes off the screen is the mode NAME beside the trigger's glyph, leaving the icon alone — for a bar where the word is a line too wide. The trigger keeps its accessible name either way, because the name is that same word rendered sr-only rather than removed.

props.name: options
props.comment: Wording for the three modes, used by the `select` and `menu` variants. Translated by default; pass your own to change the WORDS rather than just the language — an app may want "Automatic / Day / Night", which no locale file can express.

components.name: timeline
components.description: Vertical timeline of events

props.name: variant
props.comment: free-form hook written verbatim to data-wk-timeline for your own CSS; no built-in layouts

props.name: before
props.comment: show dashed fade-in line above first item

props.name: after
props.comment: show dashed fade-out line below last item

props.name: variant
props.comment: back-compat alias of `intent`

props.name: intent
props.comment: canonical color axis: default | success | warning | danger. null → falls back to `variant`

props.name: title
props.comment: The event's headline, as a prop or as the `title` slot; the slot wins when both are given.

components.name: tree-view
components.description: Hierarchical tree view

props.name: label
props.comment: Names the tree. A `role="tree"` is announced by its name and nothing else.

props.name: value
props.comment: The node's key, handed to `tree-node-select` beside its label.

components.name: video
components.description: A video in the page that plays on a press, from a file, a stream or YouTube and Vimeo after consent, or as a muted loop with a pause button

props.name: src
props.comment: A file, a stream (HLS, a playlist ending in .m3u8), or the address of a video on YouTube or Vimeo (Support\VideoSource).

props.name: title
props.comment: The video's name: the play button's, the provider player's and the notice's.

props.name: poster
props.comment: The page's own still, shown until the video plays. A provider's thumbnail would be a request to the provider, so it is never fetched.

props.name: tracks
props.comment: Captions and subtitles for a file or a stream: arrays with `src`, and `srclang`, `label`, `kind` (captions, subtitles, descriptions) and `default` as a <track> takes them.

props.name: background
props.comment: A muted loop with a pause button, which starts when it is seen.

props.name: consented
props.comment: Whether the page holds the reader's consent for the provider, and the name of that consent.

components.name: conversation
components.description: Stick-to-bottom chat transcript scroller — follow-output, unread jump-to-latest, and history anchor-preserve

props.name: label
props.comment: Accessible name for the transcript log region.

props.name: maxHeight
props.comment: Height cap of the scroll viewport. A transcript needs a bounded height — without one there is nothing to scroll and follow-output is meaningless.

props.name: threshold
props.comment: px tolerance for "at bottom". Null → the plugin default (24).

components.name: data-table
components.description: Client-mode data table with sort, search, selection, density, and column manager

props.name: rows
props.comment: row objects (client mode)

props.name: columns
props.comment: [{key,label,sortable?,sortStart?,align?,cellType?,hrefKey?,intents?,subKey?,intentKey?,avatarKey?,prominence?}] cellType: text|number|badge|badges|code|link · intents: value -> success|warning|danger|neutral hrefKey: for a link column, the ROW field holding the URL. A row without one reads as text. subKey / intentKey / avatarKey: the ROW names its second line, its intent, its avatar. prominence: strong|muted — how loud the column reads. Absent is the middle. sortStart: asc|desc — the direction of the column's first click. Absent is asc.

props.name: rowKey
props.comment: unique id field for selection + morph keying

props.name: selectable
props.comment: per-row + header selection checkboxes

props.name: stickyColumn
props.comment: Freeze the first column while the rest scroll sideways. In an overview the first column NAMES the row, and on a phone it is the first thing a swipe takes away. With `selectable` BOTH leading columns freeze — the checkbox and the name — because a checkbox that scrolls out from under its own row is worse than one that never moved. The offset is known in advance: the selection column's width is set here, by this component, at `w-10`.

props.name: searchable
props.comment: toolbar search box (client-side filter)

props.name: density
props.comment: comfortable | compact

props.name: columnManager
props.comment: show/hide-columns dropdown

props.name: hidden
props.comment: Hidden column keys. Read from the state carrier rather than `x-data`, so a render with a different list moves the table to it without rebuilding the component; the reader's own choice arrives as `wirekit:data-table-columns-changed`, for an application to keep.

props.name: server
props.comment: server-driven: stop local sort/filter, emit events only

props.name: sortKey
props.comment: The order the table starts in: a column key and a direction. In server mode, the order the server already applied, so `aria-sort` and the arrow describe the rows on screen. Without them every column would read "none" over a sorted table, and a screen reader would say so.

props.name: search
props.comment: The filter the server applied, for a server-mode table. It fills the search field on the first render (a page opened as `?q=…` shows its filter) and whenever the server changes it on its own, such as a "clear filters" control. Null leaves the field to the reader.

props.name: searchDebounce
props.comment: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before announcing `search-change`. Only the OUTBOUND event waits. `x-model` still updates on every keystroke, so the client-side filter stays instant and the box never feels laggy — what this delays is the round trip a server-mode table makes, which would otherwise be one request per CHARACTER: typing an eight-letter name would ask the application eight questions and throw away the first seven answers, each of them a query. Configurable because the right value is a property of the BACKEND, not of the table: a local index wants it short, a rate-limited third-party search wants it long. 0 disables the wait entirely, for a developer who throttles on their own side.

props.name: loading
props.comment: A wait the server declares. Server mode exists for datasets whose round trip is SLOW, and every sort click and every keystroke in the search field starts one — meanwhile the table keeps showing the previous page's rows with nothing to say a query is on its way. A sighted reader cannot tell a slow query from an ignored click, and a screen-reader user gets no WCAG 4.1.3 status until the rows change. The table marks itself busy for the round trips it starts (a sort, a search), from the moment the commit that carries one is sent until it comes back. This prop is for a wait the table cannot see: a server-side process the page is waiting on. A render that passes `true` holds the table busy until a render passes `false`.

props.name: caption
props.comment: accessible table caption / name

props.name: bulkActionsLabel
props.comment: Accessible name for the bulk-action bar, and the switch that makes it a LANDMARK. Same rule as `caption` below the table: `role="region"` plus a name is a landmark, and several tables on one page would each emit a bar called "Bulk actions" — one name across N rotor entries, which is what axe reports as `landmark-unique`. So the role waits for a name the CALLER chose. Nothing is lost without it: the bar is not a scroll region (no `overflow-*`, no `max-h-*`), so it needs no `tabindex` for WCAG 2.1.1, its controls are in the tab order on their own, and the selection count is announced through the `aria-live` span rather than through the landmark.

props.name: name
props.comment: hidden-input name mirroring the selected ids

props.name: total
props.comment: In server mode with `selectable`, the number of matches on all pages. Once the reader has selected the whole page and there are more, the bar offers every match, and `selection-change` carries `allMatches`. Read again on every render.

props.name: filter
props.comment: Anything that names the filter the server applied beyond `search`, such as a status. A render with another value, or another `search`, while every match is selected clears it.

props.name: selected
props.comment: The selection as the application holds it, beside the `wire:model` that receives it: a list of row keys. The first render opens with it; after that the table takes it only from a response that changed it, such as a bulk action that clears the list, and keeps the reader's own otherwise.

props.name: allMatches
props.comment: Every match, as the application holds it, beside `selected`.

components.name: date-separator
components.description: Horizontal divider with centered date label

components.name: event-calendar
components.description: Scheduling calendar with month, week, and agenda views

props.name: events
props.comment: [{id,title,start,end?,allDay?,intent?}]

props.name: dayMarkers
props.comment: [{date,label,type?,blocked?}] day-level holiday/working/note markers

props.name: selectableDays
props.comment: Day selection, opt-in. `selectableDays` makes each month day number a button that dispatches `wirekit:event-calendar-day-select` with the day (YYYY-MM-DD) and the ids of its events; `dayDetail` adds a built-in list of that day's events under the month grid and implies the first. Both default off: a button in every cell is a tab stop in every cell.

props.name: filterable
props.comment: One toggle per event `category`, above the views. Events without a category are never filtered. Off by default, and rendered only when the events carry two categories or more: a single chip filters nothing.

props.name: view
props.comment: month | week | agenda

props.name: date
props.comment: ISO date the calendar opens on (default today)

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.comment: 0 Sun .. 1 Mon

props.name: locale
props.comment: BCP-47 locale for every date and time the calendar prints. Null → the application locale, which is what the rest of the component is already written in. Its own prop for the one case the app locale cannot serve: a calendar showing a schedule that belongs to a different region than the page around it.

props.name: weekLabel
props.comment: Accessible name for the WEEK time-grid, and the switch that makes it a LANDMARK. Its own prop rather than a reuse of `ariaLabel`: that one names the whole calendar, and a region inheriting the widget's name announces the part as the whole. The grid's name was a hardcoded "Week schedule", so two calendars on a page produced two identical rotor entries (axe: `landmark-unique`). Unnamed, the grid keeps `tabindex="0"` and no role — reachable per WCAG 2.1.1, deliberately not a destination.

props.name: level
props.comment: Heading level for the title (1-6). Defaults to 2 — the calendar's period label — so nothing moves for a caller who never sets it. Set it to match the surrounding document outline: a component cannot know where in the page it sits, and a guessed level is worse than a chosen one. A skipped level is what `heading-order` reports, and that rule lives in axe's best-practice tag rather than the WCAG tags most suites run — so it is invisible to an axe sweep and visible in Lighthouse.

components.name: kanban
components.description: Horizontal scrollable board of status columns

props.name: crossColumn
props.comment: Cards may move BETWEEN sortable columns: dragged onto another one, or moved with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight while lifted. Opt-in, because it changes what those two keys do on this board — without it they move a lifted card within its own column, which is what every board shipped so far has taught its users.

components.name: kanban-column
components.description: Single column within a kanban board

props.name: columnId
props.comment: What the application calls this column when a card moves between columns on a `cross-column` board: it arrives as `from.column` / `to.column` in `wirekit:sortable:moved`. Without one the column is named by its position among the board's sortable columns — honest, and only usable by a server that addresses columns positionally, the same rule a card without a `data-sortable-id` follows.

components.name: message
components.description: Chat/comment message bubble with author, timestamp, and delivery status

props.name: status
props.comment: Delivery ladder for an outgoing message: sending | sent | delivered | read | failed. Null (default) renders nothing — most threads only track status on the messages the current user sent.

props.name: statusTime
props.comment: When the status was reached (Carbon|string). Given → the status glyph carries a tooltip AND its accessible text reads "Read at 9:15 AM" instead of just "Read". Formatted with the same locale-aware short time as the message timestamp (or `timeFormat`).

props.name: actionsReveal
props.comment: How the actions slot is revealed. 'hover' (default) shows it on hover OR keyboard focus; 'always' keeps it visible — the accessible path for touch (no hover) and for surfaces where the actions should always be reachable.

props.name: timeFormat
props.comment: Carbon format string for the timestamp. Null (default) renders the locale-aware short time via isoFormat('LT') — "9:15 PM" for en, "21:15" for de and other 24h locales. Pass an explicit format (e.g. 'H:i') to override.

props.name: timezone
props.comment: The zone the timestamp and the status time are written in for the reader, a name such as "Europe/Berlin". Null → the zone of the value given.

components.name: message-group
components.description: A run of messages from one sender, with the avatar and name printed once

props.name: author
props.comment: The same shape `x-wirekit::message` takes: ['name' => …, 'avatar' => …, 'role' => …]. The group prints it ONCE and the messages inside stop repeating it — that is the whole component. Each message keeps its own timestamp: a run shares a sender, not a moment. No angle brackets around a component name in this file, here or anywhere else in it. Blade's tag compiler runs over the raw source before anything understands PHP comments, so a tag written inside one is compiled as a tag — which leaves the view with a `$component->withAttributes()` call and no component, and the error names an undefined variable rather than the comment that caused it.

props.name: announce
props.comment: Announce the typing state to assistive technology. Off by default: a transcript that announces every keystroke-driven typing flicker is unusable with a screen reader. Turn it on for a one-off "assistant is working" row.

props.name: interval

props.comment: Interval-keyed amounts for a table that offers a billing toggle, e.g. :prices="['monthly' => 4900, 'annual' => 49000]". Every amount is rendered and FORMATTED SERVER-SIDE; the surrounding pricing-table's toggle only switches which one is visible, so the currency/locale/minor-unit logic is never reimplemented in JavaScript. `price` still works on its own.

props.name: period
props.comment: "mo", "year", "seat/mo" — rendered next to the amount.

props.name: periods
props.comment: Per-interval period labels, e.g. :periods="['monthly' => 'mo', 'annual' => 'yr']. Falls back to `period` for any interval not listed.

props.name: description
props.comment: Copy under the plan name.

props.name: featured
props.comment: The recommended plan. Highlighted with a badge AND a ring — never a tint alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

props.name: featuredLabel
props.comment: Text for the featured badge.

props.name: priceLabel
props.comment: Shown instead of an amount ("Let's talk") for a contact-us tier.

props.name: minorUnits
props.comment: Forwarded to the inner price component so a tier can render minor-unit amounts (e.g. 4900 -> EUR 49.00), locale-format them, and size the amount.

components.name: price
components.description: Locale-aware currency display with optional discount

props.name: from
props.comment: The amount is the lowest of several, the price of the cheapest variant of a product: a word before it, "from" in the application's language, says so on screen and to a screen reader.

props.name: maxPrecision
props.comment: At most this many decimals, for a price that has more than its currency: a price per piece such as 0.045 €. Never fewer than the currency's own, and trailing zeros drop back to them.

props.name: fit
props.comment: Shrinks the price from its size down to a floor so it fits its line: the struck price, the word "from" and the amount shrink together, the change, the suffix and the unit price keep their size. true for the `--text-wk-fit-floor` token, a length such as `8px` for a floor of its own, null or false for none.

components.name: quick-replies
components.description: Suggested replies under a message — a named group of chips that dispatch the answer the reader picked

props.name: replies
props.comment: The suggested replies, in the order they are offered. An entry is either a string — the label, which is then also the value — or an array with `label`, an optional `value` (defaults to the label) and an optional `disabled`.

props.name: label
props.comment: Names the group. A group of buttons with no name is announced as a group of nothing, so an unset label falls back to a translated default rather than to silence.

components.name: reaction
components.description: Emoji reaction pill with count and toggle state

props.name: optimistic
props.comment: The Livewire method this reaction should call, when it should show the new state before the server has agreed to it. Null leaves the component exactly as it has always rendered: server markup, no Alpine. Needs `wirekit-optimistic.js` on the page beside the bundle, as docs.wirekit.app/extending/optimistic-ui shows; without it no `wirekitOptimistic` exists.

props.name: optimisticArgs
props.comment: Extra arguments appended to the optimistic action call, after the new value. A list of identical controls — one per row — needs to tell the server WHICH row, and the optimistic layer carries that: it spreads `args` into the call.

components.name: reveal
components.description: Animation wrapper — viewport / click / manual triggers, 11 in/out presets

props.name: preset
props.comment: Animation preset name. One of 11 in-presets: fade, slide-up, slide-down, slide-left, slide-right, scale, zoom, flip, rotate, bounce, spring

props.name: trigger
props.comment: Trigger mode: 'viewport' (IntersectionObserver), 'click', or 'manual' (fires on a `wirekit:reveal` event at window: `$dispatch('wirekit:reveal')` in Alpine, or window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('wirekit:reveal'))).

props.name: duration
props.comment: Duration token: 'fast' (150ms), 'normal' (300ms, default), 'slow' (600ms).

props.name: once
props.comment: Re-fire on every trigger? Default true = animate once and stop.

props.name: threshold
props.comment: IntersectionObserver threshold (only used when trigger='viewport'). 0..1.

props.name: delay
props.comment: Delay before the entrance animation begins. One of: null   — no delay (default — animation begins immediately on trigger) 'none'/'sm'/'md'/'lg'/'xl' — token name → maps to --motion-wk-delay-* var int    — raw milliseconds (e.g. delay="125" for a custom rhythm)
