components.description: Chart drawn with Chart.js or ApexCharts, themed by the WireKit tokens

components.name: fonts
components.description: GDPR-compliant font loader

props.name: nonce
props.comment: A CSP nonce for the inline <style> below. Left out, it resolves itself from the container binding or Vite — see WireKit::cspNonce(). Pass one explicitly when the application mints a value per response and publishes it nowhere.

props.name: sans
props.comment: A family for this page in place of `wirekit.fonts.sans`, `.serif` or `.mono`: a key from the registry, of that category. Null keeps the configured one. For a font that changes per shop or per tenant without touching the config; list such families in `wirekit.fonts.publish` so they are published and keep their preload.

components.name: glass
components.description: Liquid Glass extension — include once as the first element of the layout body; takes no props and renders no slot

components.name: icon
components.description: SVG icon with preset support

components.name: map
components.description: Map adapter (MapLibre/Leaflet peer dependency) with markers and an accessible location list

props.name: center
props.comment: [lat, lng]

props.name: markers
props.comment: [{id,lat,lng,label,body?,intent?}]

props.name: provider
props.comment: maplibre | leaflet (peer dependency)

props.name: styleUrl
props.comment: tile/style URL (provider-specific)

props.name: attribution
props.comment: tile attribution HTML, e.g. '© OpenStreetMap contributors' — shown by Leaflet's attribution control; required by some tile sources (OSM)

props.name: height
props.comment: map canvas height (CSS length)

props.name: reducedData
props.comment: 'respect' (default) | 'ignore' — what to do when the reader's browser reports `prefers-reduced-data: reduce`. Tiles are the largest network cost this library can cause and the only one it controls at runtime: a map fetches tile after tile as it settles, and again on every pan. Nothing else WireKit ships fetches on every interaction the way a map does — the stylesheet contains no `url()` at all — so this is where the preference can actually be honored rather than merely acknowledged. On 'respect' the canvas is withheld and the marker list carries the content, with a control to load the map anyway. Use 'ignore' where the canvas IS the content rather than an illustration of it — a delivery-tracking view, a route editor.

props.name: listLabel
props.comment: Heading above the marker list — and the switch that makes that list a LANDMARK. The visible heading is ALWAYS rendered, so the fallback survives as a resolved variable; only the `role="region"` waits for a caller-supplied name. A fallback name such as "Locations" would make every map on a store-locator page the same rotor entry (axe: `landmark-unique`).

props.name: list
props.comment: Show the marker-list sidebar. Set list="false" for a map-only surface — the list stays in the DOM as an sr-only accessible companion (a map is opaque to assistive tech, so the locations must remain reachable), only the visual sidebar is hidden and the canvas fills the width.

props.name: highlight
props.comment: Selected-row highlight: 'ring' (inset frame — the default) or 'fill' (tinted row background), colored via highlightColor (intent vocabulary). Both variants are demonstrated side by side on the docs MapLibre page.

components.name: structured-data
components.description: JSON-LD script block emitter (XSS-safe via JSON_HEX_TAG)

props.name: nonce
props.comment: A CSP nonce for the JSON-LD block below. Left out, it resolves itself from the container binding or Vite — see WireKit::cspNonce(). Pass one explicitly when the application mints a value per response and publishes it nowhere. A JSON-LD block is a data block: the HTML standard stops preparing a <script> whose type is not a script type before it consults the Content Security Policy, so `script-src` does not apply to it and no policy can reject it. The attribute is harmless there, and it costs one string when a nonce exists and nothing at all when it does not.
